item.title: Friday, November 13, 2026
item.description:
The LZ event, read elastically

Since September, almost every model of the 248 keV LZ recoil has used inelastic scattering, and each one has been built to survive solar capture. Bera et al. arXiv:2611.15957 drop the mass splitting entirely. Their dark matter is a Majorana fermion whose only electromagnetic interaction is an anapole moment, and the momentum dependence alone hardens the recoil spectrum enough to fit the event. The same coupling gives the relic abundance at ~300 GeV, and the model predicts more events at lower energies, which the full LZ run will test. The abstract checks collider and indirect-detection limits but doesn’t mention solar capture, which is where earlier readings of this event were excluded. Lin et al. arXiv:2611.16689 recompute solar capture itself, and Dai et al. arXiv:2611.16553 add a gauged B-L two-scalar model with a three-bin likelihood fit; the 11-03 Higgs-portal model gave rate estimates but no likelihood.

Themes

Loop counts go up

  • Li et al. arXiv:2611.15366 compute QED charge, mass and field renormalization analytically at six loops for arbitrary N_f, and say the methods open the way to six-loop QCD.
  • Gehrmann et al. arXiv:2611.15836 give full-color three-loop V+jet amplitudes, whose finite remainders live in a much smaller function space than the underlying integrals.
  • Two results aimed at lepton colliders: Haisch et al. arXiv:2611.15807 compute S and T at two loops in the Z_2 singlet model three independent ways, and Devoto et al. arXiv:2611.17171 supply two-loop mixed QCD–EW corrections to e⁺e⁻→bb̅.

This continues September’s precision-QCD run, now carried into electroweak observables.

Grover for haloscopes

Bogorad et al. arXiv:2611.14641 show that wavelike dark matter can act as a repeatable phase gate over many coherence times. A Grover search over N_bins frequency bins then gains a factor of √(N_bins). Bao et al. arXiv:2611.14629 work out a transmon version; reaching the QCD axion band takes 10⁶ entangled qubits. Soto Alcaraz et al. arXiv:2611.15878 use a two-node quantum network to tell an isotropic halo from a Gaia-like anisotropic one, which works only once Earth’s rotation sweeps the baseline across the sky. This adds a quantum-algorithm route to the haloscope readout work covered on 11-05.

Supercooling, with consistency checks

Zhang et al. arXiv:2611.14593 find that three different criteria for a transition completing share the same boundary. Close to that boundary, though, a homogeneous cosmology can’t be justified, so the claimed arbitrarily strong monopole suppression doesn’t hold up. Chaudhuri arXiv:2611.16845 finds a fast, strongly supercooled electroweak step in scale-invariant models. The LISA signal depends on the acoustic GW description still applying in that regime. Cassidy et al. arXiv:2611.15856 find that GW and di-Higgs predictions survive added dimension-six operators, but the Higgs trilinear does not. Same lesson as 11-03: a GW forecast is only as good as its transition dynamics.

Top SMEFT, two ways to slice

ATLAS arXiv:2611.16347 fits 33 Wilson coefficients across nine top-associated processes and sees no significant deviation. It also compares generic object-counting categories with process-targeted regions; the targeted regions give better sensitivity for most coefficients. Kumari et al. arXiv:2611.15274 make a parallel point about taggers. Taggers with similar AUC differ by up to 3× in discovery significance on CMS Open Data, and the particle transformers extend the Z’ mass reach by 400 GeV.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.15957: The first minimal elastic fit to the LZ event, with a relic-density coincidence and a falsifiable prediction at lower recoil energies.
  • arXiv:2611.16689: Solar capture, the constraint every LZ model has designed around since Pospelov, recomputed with a transport equation. When nuclear scattering is rare, captured DM never thermalizes and annihilation drops by orders of magnitude. For the inelastic higgsino, though, the bound on the splitting tightens by tens of keV.
  • arXiv:2611.16347: A template for multi-process SMEFT fits, with a direct head-to-head of categorization strategies.
  • arXiv:2611.14641: The cleanest argument yet that quantum algorithms can get around the coherence-time limit in dark-matter searches.
  • arXiv:2611.16544: Liu proves that Craig’s overlap measure and the Hsu/Witten continuum determinant agree for one SU(5) generation on T⁴, up to a local counterterm. This is the comparison Witten’s 11-05 note invited.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.16530 New measurement of BR(K⁺→π⁺νν̅) at the NA62 experiment — Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). The 2023–24 data double the sample. The abstract gives only the expected 5σ SM sensitivity, not the measured value.
  • arXiv:2611.15869 Discovering new physics with semitauonic b-hadron decays — Markus Prim et al. (hep-ph). A review arriving after Belle II’s September result eased the R(D^*) tension.
  • arXiv:2611.14616 N_eff, Radiative Dirac Neutrinos, and Flavor Physics from Leptoquarks — Patricio Escalona et al. (hep-ph). Fits the Belle II K⁺νν̅ excess, with N_eff bounds that can beat collider limits.
  • arXiv:2611.16715 Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth’s Mantle… — Michael Leyton et al. (physics.geo-ph). Across ~3 million fits, no mantle model reproduces the Kamioka–Jiangmen geo-neutrino gap. The authors conclude it is a local effect or statistical scatter.
  • arXiv:2611.16684 Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD? — Zi-Hao Liu et al. (hep-th). No: light-quark spin damps at the transport rate, which undercuts treating spin as a slow hydrodynamic variable.

item.title: Wednesday, November 11, 2026
item.description:
A 1.9σ ordering, taken apart

The combined reactor plus ν_μ-disappearance fit disfavors inverted ordering at 1.9σ. Machado et al. arXiv:2611.13629 show that number is a balance of small pulls that disagree with each other. Reactor+T2K and reactor+NOvA point to opposite orderings, and the two experiments’ Δm² values differ by ~3.5%, about the size of the ordering effect itself. More JUNO data tops out near 3σ. Beyond that, the limiting factor is ν_μ energy reconstruction, which means neutrino–nucleus modeling at the percent level, so today’s interaction-physics papers matter more than usual.

Themes

Interaction modeling sets the limit

Two papers sit right behind Machado’s conclusion. Ježo et al. arXiv:2611.13618 compute heavy-quark F_4 and F_5 at NLO in APFEL++. They find these structure functions suppress the CC ν_τ cross section by up to 40% near the kinematic boundary, the first such estimate for SHiP, IceCube and DUNE. Fatima et al. arXiv:2611.13602 find that medium effects and final-state interactions substantially suppress η production on C and Ar. Both extend the 11-02 generator-rebuilding thread, which now has a concrete percent-level target.

Light-field bounds, recalibrated

  • Pseudo-Goldstone couplings. Banerjee et al. arXiv:2611.14473 point out that linear-coupling bounds fail once a pNGB reaches O(f) near its source. As a result, terrestrial fifth-force and equivalence-principle tests lose their low-mass reach.
  • SPHEREx axion limits. Hainje et al. arXiv:2611.13090 set the first SPHEREx ALP limits over 0.5–3.3 eV, overlapping the window JWST closed to QCD-axion dark matter in September. Their best limit is g_aγγ<2.1×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹, and their own Cramér–Rao estimate says better methods alone could improve it more than 10×.
  • Helioscope mirrors. Frerick arXiv:2611.13073 shows that helioscope mirrors convert the longitudinal solar dark-photon flux that conventional searches miss.

Precision plumbing

  • IR finiteness without dim reg. Capatti et al. arXiv:2611.13184 build an initial-state KLN construction compatible with collinear factorisation. It produces IR-finite partonic cross sections in four dimensions by Monte Carlo, demonstrated at NLO for Drell–Yan and tt̅.
  • A published correction. The same group’s comment arXiv:2611.13087 argues that a 2024 PRL on vacuum-amplitude cross sections gets both its central claims wrong.
  • B→X_sγ uncertainty. Bartocci et al. arXiv:2611.14318 complete NLO for the resolved Q_1–Q_7γ term at m_c→0. This is one of the leading uncertainties in the SM B→X_sγ prediction, which August’s exact-m_c NNLO work had brought into line with data.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.13629: Which data pairings pull which way. A shift of 3.5% in a single experiment reverses the preference, so check this before quoting any ordering result.
  • arXiv:2611.14473: Above a few×10⁻¹² eV, nothing constrains a >10-decade span of nucleon coupling. The paper names a ground–space clock comparison as the test.
  • arXiv:2611.13617: Dutta’s MeV lepton-number-breaking scalar doubles as the SIDM mediator and decays to neutrinos at a rate fixed by neutrino masses. It is fit to dwarf-to-cluster data, not lensing, yet lands near Gilman’s 11-02 neutrinophilic-scalar corner. It prefers normal ordering.
  • arXiv:2611.13833: Rubtsov et al. find an atmospheric-muon excess that is consistent across four experiments. It calls for more energetic muon parents early in the cascade, not extra soft multiplicity, which discriminates between proposed muon-puzzle fixes.
  • arXiv:2611.13184: Local Unitarity reaches hadron colliders with a universal MS conversion.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.13583 Active learning at a graduate summer school… — Nicholas Kamp et al. (physics.ed-ph). Six lecturers new to active learning had about four hours of preparation, and afterward 33 of 36 students wanted more of it.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.14335 Search for heavy top quark partners with charge 5/3… — CMS Collaboration (hep-ex). Limits reach 1630 GeV for decays to tW. This is also the first search in the tH^± mode.
  • arXiv:2611.14103 Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD… — Constantia Alexandrou et al. (hep-lat). They find σ_πN=53.0(7.4)(1.6) MeV, extending yesterday’s g_A result on four spacings at physical pion mass.
  • arXiv:2611.13222 AlphaHits… — Sascha Caron et al. (hep-ex). The model reconstructs tracks directly from hits with a TrackML score of 0.959, the best reported for inclusive full-detector reconstruction.
  • arXiv:2611.14331 Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter — Tyler Gorda et al. (nucl-th). Extending the pQCD bound to finite temperature excludes seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models by ŝ=4.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.13629 — Where does the neutrino Mass Ordering preference come from? (Pedro A. N. Machado et al.)

The combined reactor + ν_μ-disappearance fit disfavors IO at 1.9σ (CL_s, pseudo-experiments), but the pieces disagree. JUNO’s 207 days alone favor NO by Δχ²⁼¹.84. Forcing JUNO from its low global minimum (1.96×10⁻³ eV² in NO) onto Daya Bay’s branch near 2.5×10⁻³ costs 5.6 units in NO and 4.0 in IO, so reactors alone give T_MO=0.21, which is no preference. Each ν_μ experiment pulls a different way. Reactor+NOvA disfavors IO at 1.4σ, while reactor+T2K disfavors NO at 0.8σ. The T2K–NOvA gap in |Δm²_31| is about 3.5% (~1σ), comparable to the 1.6–3.2% Δm²_ee–Δm²_μμ separation that distinguishes the orderings. In a stress test, sliding T2K onto NOvA’s best fit gives a 1.8σ IO rejection, while the reverse gives a 1.7σ NO rejection. The cosδ_CP term contributes at most 0.4%, so it cannot explain the gap. Asimov projections stall the reactor contribution: 1500 more JUNO days yield 2.8σ, and a perfect reactor measurement asymptotes at 2.9σ.

Why it matters. Past ~3σ this channel is limited by ν_μ energy reconstruction at the percent level. That is the target for today’s interaction-modeling papers, and the same requirement applies to HK. DUNE’s matter-effect route sidesteps it.

Caveats. The shift exercise simply sums χ² curves and ignores the experiments’ shared δ_CP/θ_23 dependence. The known appearance-channel disagreement may leak into the Δm² values. The statistics also matter: naive √(T) would claim a 3.1σ IO tension where toys give 1.8σ.

arXiv:2611.14473 — Running out of Field Range: Nonlinear Sourcing of Light Scalars (Abhishek Banerjee et al.)

For a pNGB with periodic potential and coupling, matter induces m_ρ²∝dQρ/f and drives θ→π/2. This caps the sourced field at πf/2 and suppresses the local linear coupling as cosθ. For the photon coupling the Earth saturates at d_e≃2.2×10⁻⁹⁽f/10 MeV), about 10⁴ below the MICROSCOPE linear limit. The two become comparable only near f∼100 GeV, so existing bounds sit outside their own validity regime. At f=10 MeV the recast results are:

  • MICROSCOPE: at orbit cosθ≃0.16, and the limit relaxes to d_e≲2.8, a factor 7×10⁴ weaker. It closes again near 3×10⁹ as the satellite walls screen the field.
  • Electron and nucleon couplings: d_m_e≲170 and d_m_N≲6, weakened by 2×10⁵ and 2×10⁶.
  • Eöt-Wash uranium test: develops a vertical wall below m_0=3×10⁻¹¹ eV once the air is sourced. MICROSCOPE loses reach above a few×10⁻¹² eV, leaving an unconstrained mass window between the two.
  • Stellar bounds: linear cooling bounds vanish because cores also saturate. Only quadratic pair emission survives, e.g. SN 1987A gives d_e≲4×10⁹.

A ground–ISS clock comparison measures field values rather than gradients. With ACES Cs/H-maser it would reach d_e≳4×10⁴ above 1/h_ISS, with a ceiling near 10⁶ set by the ISS’s own sourcing. A ²²⁹Th clock would reach ∼3×10⁻².

Caveats. The upper edges depend on geometry. The lab rock opens a notch in the uranium exclusion, the satellite is a toy model, and LAGEOS–Lunar is ambiguous at this f. Naturalness also needs a ℤ_N to avoid vacuum sourcing.

arXiv:2611.13617 — Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking (Manoranjan Dutta)

One MeV-scale L-breaking vev generates μ_S for the inverse seesaw and a pseudo-Dirac splitting for DM. A structural result follows: any central coupling satisfies |g|≃Δm_χ/(2v_ϕ), so a vev-generated splitting cannot support strong inelastic SIDM. In the viable symmetric regime, Δm_χ≃2g_11v_ϕ is tens of MeV and scattering is elastic.

With α_11 fixed by the relic density (decoupled, hotter dark sector) and exact partial waves including Majorana statistics, the fit is:

  • Main band: m_s≃1.9 MeV×(m_χ/GeV), with best fit m_χ=7.6 GeV, m_s=14.6 MeV and χ²/dof=2.04. The data’s own floor is ~1.9, since a free power law gets 1.92.
  • Resonant islands: appear at higher mass.
  • Overall range: 3–70 GeV at 95% CL, with m_s = 6–28 MeV.

The mediator decays to νν in roughly 40 ms at a rate fixed by ∑m_ν². That lifetime and SN 1987A confine v_ϕ to roughly 130–390 MeV. NO is preferred because its ν_3-dominated couplings weaken the SN bound by F=5.7, while IO (F≃1) forces m_s≲6 MeV, against N_eff.

Why it matters. It is a concrete NO-predicting model, landing as Machado shows how fragile the current oscillation NO hint is. CMB-S4-level N_eff would probe m_s≲11 MeV.

Caveats. The 70 GeV cap depends on thermal history; it falls to ~60 GeV at a common temperature. The SN treatment is one-zone and ignores flavor conversion in the envelope.

(Full texts for arXiv:2611.13833 and arXiv:2611.13184 were not supplied, so they are not expanded here.)

item.title: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
item.description:
LEP’s neutrino count, recounted

Madison arXiv:2611.12265 rebuilds LEP beam–beam effects in a new framework, FeeBL, and finds a ~2% bias in the published beam-deflection simulations behind the Bhabha luminosity.

  • The correction: N_ν=2.9965±0.0040, against 2.9963±0.0074. The central value barely moves and the error nearly halves.
  • The condition: the smaller error holds only under an assumed common rescaling of experiment-specific uncertainties, which the author says needs further scrutiny.
  • FCC-ee: monochromatizing toward s-channel Higgs would need ~10 m of horizontal dispersion. That is a sobering number for last week’s FCC-ee-as-arbiter thread.

The rest of the day is spread thin: lattice nucleon structure, light-ion quenching, an 11σ strange vector, and several papers that say exactly where their own fits stop being trustworthy.

Themes

Fits that state their limits

  • Lattice estimators. Moerschbacher et al. arXiv:2611.10773 find that covariance-optimized background-field estimators gain 1–2% in precision. Their weights, however, carry 10³–10⁴× more leverage on omitted response modes than fixed stencils do.
  • Glueball sum rules. Kang et al. arXiv:2611.12073 separate “a pole fits” from “this region is required.” For the 0⁻⁺ current, the band containing X(2370) can be empty while a broader band must carry ~44% of the spectrum.
  • tt̅j resummation. Chargeishvili arXiv:2611.11600 corrects the tt̅j soft anomalous dimensions, then keeps NLO as his central prediction because his own NNLL kernel fails beyond 100–200 GeV of emitted energy.

This is last week’s identifiability-audit habit (Serao’s blind directions, Shen’s magic measures), now spreading into lattice and perturbative QCD.

One QGP, oxygen to lead?

Karmakar et al. arXiv:2611.12404 run DREENA with a single parameter set across O, Ne, Xe and Pb and reproduce the observed suppression ordering. They predict that v_2^SP/(1-R_AA) is nearly flat in p_⊥ for light ions, which is a clean test.

Yang et al. arXiv:2611.11347 describe φ and Ω v_2 by recombination from 7.7 GeV to 5.02 TeV. At LHC energies, though, the extracted strange-quark v_2 exceeds the NCQ-scaled value. That is worth remembering before reading ALICE’s O–O φ result (10-28) through simple scaling.

Strange vector, compact T_cc

BESIII arXiv:2611.11328 observes a 1⁻ K_1^*(1870) in Kη’ at 11.0σ, with Γ≈167 MeV, and pitches it as input for hybrid searches. Peng et al. arXiv:2611.11472 fix the contact interaction from the T_cc pole and find the X(3872) comes out 5–12 MeV too deeply bound. Their Feshbach analysis instead reads T_cc as mixing with a compact ccu̅d̅ state.

Nucleon structure, lattice-anchored

  • Charges. Alexandrou et al. arXiv:2611.10816 get g_A^u-d=1.263(34)(26) from four spacings at physical masses, including disconnected isoscalar pieces.
  • PDFs. Gao et al. arXiv:2611.12730 find the isovector PDF matches phenomenology for 0.25≲|x|≲0.75. For the first time, the imaginary part agrees too.
  • Transversity. Dong et al. arXiv:2611.12745 add x-dependent lattice transversity to a dihadron fit, and the down-valence distribution moves past the Soffer bound.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.12265 (Madison): A legacy precision number re-examined with new code. Read the uncertainty argument before quoting ±0.0040.
  • arXiv:2611.11328 (BESIII): A new strange 1⁻ at 11σ, in a channel built for hybrid hunting.
  • arXiv:2611.12774 (Takeuchi et al.): Broadband receivers instead of a cavity give χ<(3.1–17)×10⁻¹² over 18–38.5 GHz. That is more than 10× better over most of 74–110 μeV, plus first direct limits up to 159 μeV.
  • arXiv:2611.10773 (Moerschbacher et al.): Exact decuplet ratios serve as built-in controls. The correlated fit misses them by 3–17%, while the fixed stencils pass, so precision and robustness are separate axes.
  • arXiv:2611.10115 (Fei et al.): A training-free greedy search recovers Parke–Taylor from all 1024 Feynman-diagram forms. It generally beats published ML simplifiers on solve rate, at 0.02–0.3 s per case with finite-field checks.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.11458 After the Higgs: Looking for the Universe Behind the Particle — Veronica Sanz (hep-ph). How to plan with no guaranteed discovery: pursue precision without pre-picking winners, and protect theoretical risk-taking.
  • arXiv:2611.10041 Physics in Safety and Safety in Physics… — Alexander S. Sakharov (physics.acc-ph). Treats safety at ATLAS/CMS as a “safe operational phase space,” aimed at the design of HL-LHC, FCC and a muon collider.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.11957 Measurements of CP violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II — Jaeyoung Kim (on behalf of the Belle II Collaboration) (hep-ex). Every asymmetry is consistent with zero, including K⁰_SK⁰_S, one of the modes Buccella et al. targeted on 11-04. Charm CPV stays open.
  • arXiv:2611.10218 B→ invisible decays as probes of light new physics — Martín Novoa-Brunet (hep-ph). Missing-mass fits to the Belle II K⁺+invisible excess favour a two-body state near 2.1 GeV.
  • arXiv:2611.10273 Constraints on quirks from a Geant4-based reinterpretation… — Tamas Almos Vami (hep-ph). Excludes up to 870–990 GeV at Λ≲70 eV, with no sensitivity in the intermediate-Λ regime.
  • arXiv:2611.12808 First demonstration of long-distance electron drift in liquid xenon… — N. Angelides et al. (physics.ins-det). Demonstrates 2.6 m of electron drift, a benchmark for XLZD.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.12265 — Beam-beam effects on measurements at electron-positron colliders: LEP neutrino counting and Higgs factories (Brendon Madison)

The bias is real but small in N_ν; the error-bar argument is the real claim. FeeBL, a Guinea-Pig++ descendant, reproduces the analytic field-integration Bhabha deflections at LEP: inner 13.12±0.08 vs 13.09 μrad, outer 11.49±0.06 vs 11.49 μrad. The published Guinea-Pig values sit 2.2±0.5% and 2.6±0.6% low. This moves the acceptance correction from −0.10425% to −0.10671% and shifts N_ν by only +0.0002. The author cannot identify the origin of the deficit without the original settings.

The error-bar change is a separate, statistical argument. The four LEP determinations scatter less than their quoted errors allow, with a χ² lower-tail probability of 2.05%. Rescaling only the experiment-specific uncertainties by a common factor gives σ = 0.00401, with a 68% interval of [0.00391, 0.00485]. The paper explicitly says this needs each experiment’s uncertainty budget to be redone before anyone can defend quoting it. The suspected culprit is the σ⁰_had–R_ℓ correlation.

The paper also does two other things: - Beam-pair fixes. It corrects implementation defects in Guinea-Pig++ v1.2.2 pair production. The Born normalization is 1.319% low, small-angle sampling is truncated, and virtual-virtual Landau–Lifshitz collisions are dropped. - Monochromatization. Opposite horizontal dispersion narrows the ILC/LCF and HALHF peaks about 2× at constant luminosity. It reaches sub-MeV FWHM, but only at about 0.07% of nominal luminosity. FCC-ee at |D| = 175 mm is still at 57 MeV FWHM, roughly 14× wider than 4 MeV.

The ~10 m figure for FCC-ee is an extrapolation from a rigid-Gaussian model. That model already misses the FCC-ee simulation by 55% in luminosity and 22% in width. Convergence is explicitly not claimed anywhere in the paper.

arXiv:2611.11328 — Observation of a strange J^P=1⁻ resonance K^*_1(1870) in χ_c1→K⁺K⁻η^’ decays (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

A new 1⁻ state appears in Kη’ in BESIII’s ψ(2S)→γχ_c1 data. The sample is 2.71×10⁹ ψ(2S), with η′ reconstructed in both ππγ and ππη. The state is required beyond the PDG-based amplitude set, with M = 1869.0±14.6±18.6 MeV and Γ = 167.3±34.0±24.2 MeV. Its significance is 11.0σ (statistical) for 1⁻, against 3.2σ for 0⁺ and 3.7σ for 2⁺. The product branching fraction is (1.48±0.30±0.33)×10⁻⁵, and B(χ_c1→K⁺K⁻η′) = (7.90±0.48)×10⁻⁴ supersedes the earlier BESIII value.

Why it matters: this is the strangeness slot of the 1⁻⁽⁺⁾ nonet that the π₁(1600) and η₁(1855) candidates point to. One scenario predicts a strange hybrid at 1.83–1.90 GeV that couples to Kη’. Quark-model 3³S_1 expectations sit near 1.95 GeV with Kη’ suppressed, or else are implausibly broad.

Caveats: - The quoted significance is statistical only. - Several neighbours are fixed to PDG values, including K(1680) at 1718/320 MeV, so correlations with the new 1⁻ are only partly probed. - J^P=1⁻ alone cannot separate a hybrid from a conventional excited K. The collaboration says further study is needed.

arXiv:2611.12774 — Search for Dark Photon Dark Matter at 74–159 μeV/c² Using Broadband Cryogenic Receivers (Hiroki Takeuchi et al.)

No signal is seen, giving χ < (3.1–17)×10⁻¹² at 95% CL over 99.8% of 18–38.5 GHz. The setup is a metal plate viewed by cryogenic K- and Ka-band horns, with system temperatures of about 40–120 K. The readout is dSpec, a 4 GHz, 15.6 kHz-bin spectrometer that gives 2000× more integration per bin than the collaboration’s previous spectrum analyzer, for 4.8×10⁵ s per bin. The largest local excess is 4.96σ at 37.585 GHz, which becomes a global p = 0.38 once the look-elsewhere effect is included (N_eff = 1.94×10⁶).

Why it matters: the result improves the collaboration’s own limits more than 10× over most of 74–110 μeV. It also gives the first direct limits over most of 110–159 μeV, about two orders below cosmological bounds. That is the mass range where inflationary DPDM points, and resonant searches have to tune step by step to cover it.

Caveats: - The limits assume DPDM is all of the local dark matter (ρ = 0.39 GeV/cm³) with randomly oriented polarization in a single-polarization receiver. - Coherent conversion from other metal surfaces has an unknown phase. A_eff is therefore set to its minimum over that phase, which costs up to 44% in area. - Window geometry contributes up to about 25% systematic uncertainty on χ. - Clock-harmonic spurs are excluded. In those excluded intervals the conservative limit degrades to 3.8×10⁻¹⁰.

item.title: Monday, November 9, 2026
item.description:
A perturbative answer at the tt̅ threshold

Re arXiv:2611.09299 argues that threshold-sensitive top observables, meaning spin correlations and m_tt̅ near 2m_t, can be predicted reliably by keeping the first few powers of α_s/v. Reweighting nominal Monte Carlo this way agrees with data. That is the QCD side of the toponium-vs-CP-odd-Higgs question behind CMS’s threshold excess. Last week’s NNLO toponium cross section and the 2HDM interference tool were built to settle the same question. The other clean result is a negative: realistic nuclear structure does not rescue a proposed fix for the gallium anomaly. The rest of the 43 papers are mostly theory and detector design.

Themes

Top threshold, three angles

Alongside Re, Aushev et al. arXiv:2611.09797 use CMS Open Data to reach 30 GeV m_tt̅ resolution near threshold in dileptons. ML beats analytic reconstruction by ~30%, and the authors flag the νν̅ approximation as the limiting factor. Djouadi et al. arXiv:2611.09666 show that signal–background interference raises low-tanβ MSSM H/A rates by up to tens of percent. Current limits barely move, but HL-LHC mass ranges will. Taken together: the scalar reading needs interference handled properly, and the bound-state reading may need less new machinery than assumed.

Neutrino anomalies and relations

Castillo et al. arXiv:2611.09788 test a recent non-factorization proposal for the gallium deficit with shell-model transition densities. The cross section still comes out 20% above measurement. Xing arXiv:2611.09478 conjectures θ_23=(θ_12+θ_13)/2+π/8, which predicts 43.46^∘ from JUNO and Daya Bay inputs. It is numerology, but cheap to falsify. Choi et al. arXiv:2611.09037 find that strong flavor-dependent ν–DM potentials in the TXS 0506+056 spike relax IceCube flavor limits by up to four orders of magnitude.

Quantum resources, audited

Shen et al. arXiv:2611.08586 show that “minimal magic” predictions depend on which magic measure is used. That is the quantity behind the year’s “quantum magic in EW scattering” thread. Bleau et al. arXiv:2611.08595 confirm that mean-field neutrino oscillations match full multiparticle simulation at large N. That undercuts the case for quantum advantage except in the special configurations they identify. Both fit last month’s warning that standard tomography may fail at NLO: quantum-information claims in HEP are now being checked by their own community.

Nuclear structure in the initial state

Zakharov arXiv:2611.09404 adds collective quadrupole and octupole vibrations to ²⁰⁸Pb and claims this resolves the ultracentral v_2-to-v_3 puzzle. This extends last week’s light-ion finding that flow eccentricities respond to nuclear forces, now applied to the heaviest system. Barata et al. arXiv:2611.08579 separate broadening, radiation and medium response in the back-to-back dijet TEEC.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.09299 (Re): Perturbative threshold predictions that can be applied event by event. Read before attributing the excess to anything elementary.
  • arXiv:2611.09788 (Castillo et al.): Fixing gallium would need fine-tuned densities with percent-level cancellations, orders of magnitude larger than the shell model gives.
  • arXiv:2611.08586 (Shen et al.): Two measures give sin²θ_W=1/4 at all energies, while the min-relative entropy runs with energy. The physics conclusion depends on the measure.
  • arXiv:2611.09404 (Zakharov): ϵ_2{2}/ϵ_3{2}≈0.68–0.79 once Pb vibrations are included. A simple test of a long-standing puzzle.
  • arXiv:2611.09150 (Ding et al.): The lattice topological susceptibility goes from linear to quadratic in m_l through the crossover, extracted from single ensembles. The axion-mass relevance is my inference, not the authors’ claim.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.08583 DarkMatterFM-Registry… — Ioana A. Zelko et al. (astro-ph.CO). An LLM-extracted registry of 6,145 dark-matter model cards plus a 25-project roadmap. It concludes the bottleneck is shared infrastructure, not theory.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.09408 Parton density functions for future electron-positron colliders — Andrej Arbuzov et al. (hep-ph). A review of QED-PDF ISR resummation, stressing slow convergence and pair production. Relevant to last week’s KKMC/SHERPA radiative-return work.
  • arXiv:2611.08606 Just CaloCHILL… — Henry Day-Hall et al. (physics.ins-det). Latent-space hadronic shower generation, timing included, 600× faster than its predecessor.
  • arXiv:2611.09893 Challenges for minimal warm inflation… — Anish Ghoshal et al. (hep-ph). A Peccei–Quinn embedding needs an anomaly coefficient ≳100, which puts a Landau pole in QCD.
  • arXiv:2611.08514 The Koto II experiment — Silvia Martellotti (hep-ex). Targets sub-10⁻¹² sensitivity to K_L→π⁰νν̅ in the 2030s.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.09299 — Spin Correlations in tt̅ Production and Decay at the LHC in Perturbative QCD (Emanuele Re)

Bound-state effects near 2m_t can be computed in ordinary perturbative QCD, provided the observable integrates over M_tt̅ up to a cut at least ~5 GeV above threshold. The argument rests on the integrated spectral density. Bound-state poles enter at relative 𝒪(a_1³⁾, i.e. N³LO, and combine with a continuum term into an analytic result. The consequence is concrete: once the full expansion is kept, the naive toponium contribution is cut by a factor of two. Adding an η_t term on top of a perturbative continuum therefore double-counts. Re keeps the first few α_s/v terms of the Sommerfeld expansion, with a Coulomb scale of several tens of GeV set by the cut rather than by v→0, and matches them to NLO+PS and NNLO+PS. This pushes NLO+PS predictions for the spin observable D toward the ATLAS/CMS data. The shift is smaller on top of NNLO, which already contains the leading enhanced terms. For CMS’s 2018 dσ/dM_tt̅, the 𝒪(α_s³⁾ terms are “useful, but not crucial” once NNLO is included.

These are proceedings. The companion paper builds three POWHEG generators: hvq‑thr1 (narrow width), hvq‑thr2 (off-shell), and an upgraded bb4l. Their spread gives an estimate of the narrow-width-approximation uncertainty. In the thr2 comparison, the threshold increment is 1.62 pb against 2.73±0.61 pb from Garzelli et al. at M_cut=345 GeV. The two converge by about 350 GeV. Caveats: the claim fails for measurements fine enough to resolve the peak, and the author flags the newer, more exclusive CMS/ATLAS M_tt̅ analyses as possibly changing the conclusion.

arXiv:2611.09788 — Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities (D. Castillo et al.)

A recent PRL claimed that dropping lepton–nuclear factorization resolves the gallium anomaly. This paper finds that the claim does not survive realistic nuclear structure. The authors run nine shell-model calculations of the Gamow–Teller radial transition density for ⁷¹Ga↔⁷¹Ge. These span four pf g_9/2 Hamiltonians, bare and effective GT operators, and an LNPS space extended to 0f_7/2. All are normalized to the ⁷¹Ge EC half-life, 11.465±0.003 d, and convolved with Dirac–Hartree–Fock–Slater electron wavefunctions. The densities form a narrow band. The unfactorized cross sections are 5.26±0.01 (⁵¹Cr) and 6.30±0.01 (³⁷Ar) ×10⁻⁴⁵ cm², against measured values of 4.44±0.33 and 5.21±0.72. That gives experiment/theory ≈ 0.83, and the factorized and unfactorized results agree to ~1%. This is expected, since the Fermi function varies by only ~3% across the nucleus.

The PRL’s fitted densities (mDG, mTG) have overall scales 100× and 1000× the shell-model ones. Their nodes cancel so strongly that the net integral is only 2.5% and 0.25% of the integrated absolute value. Refitting with a shell-model radial ansatz requires coefficients ~3000× the calculated ones, again with percent-level cancellation. Caveats: a harmonic-oscillator radial basis is used, and q_EC absorbs two-body currents, weak magnetism and radiative corrections. The authors argue these are subleading but call for ab initio (VS-IMSRG) cross-checks. The result is consistent with the solar-source analysis, which shows no deficit.

arXiv:2611.08586 — Magic Is in the Eye of the Measure (Zhi-Heng Shen et al.)

For two qubits, “maximal magic” depends on the measure, and so does the minimal-magic determination of sin²θ_W. The paper proves global maxima exactly for four measures: - M_2: log_2(16/7) on 480 states, certified by a sum-of-squares argument. - 𝔇_min and 𝔇_max: a shared maximum log_2[6/(2+√(3))]≈0.685 on 640 states, certified by branch-and-bound over ~4.4×10⁶ boxes. - LR: log_2[(1+√(5))/2] on a continuum of 192 planes, certified by LP vertex enumeration over 626,626 vertices.

The three maximizer sets are mutually disjoint.

In tree-level Møller scattering, M_2 is minimized at s_W²⁼⁰.2317 at m_Z (measured value 0.23122) and tracks the MS running to ~1 TeV. 𝔇_min has a shallow minimum 7% low at m_Z. 𝔇_max and LR instead give a cusp at exactly 1/4 at every energy. The cause is structural. These two measures are maxima over witnesses, so their kinks point upward, and they grow linearly in |g_V| near stabilizer states. At g_V=0 the singlet scatters into itself, which pins the minimum there. One of the authors (Yin) co-authored the original Møller minimal-magic paper, so this is an internal audit. The authors stress that both the 1/4 pinning and the 𝔇_min kinks rest on exact tree-level properties and may not survive higher orders.

Full texts for arXiv:2611.09404 (Zakharov) and arXiv:2611.09150 (Ding et al.) were not supplied, so they have no deep-dive entries.

item.title: Friday, November 6, 2026
item.description:
No neutrino route to birefringence

Reig arXiv:2611.07578 tests the proposal that photons couple to the cosmic neutrino-asymmetry current, and finds it cannot produce the hinted isotropic CMB polarization rotation. That hint stands at 4.8σ, or 3.5σ after dust, and has been read as an axion Chern–Simons effect if real. The argument runs in three steps:

  • Gauge invariance forces a Kalb–Ramond field dual to a massless axion.
  • The signal then fixes g_aγ/f_ℓ at Λ_*≃10 TeV.
  • SU(2)_L fixes an electron coupling that g_e-2 plus light-shining-through-wall searches already exclude, as does stellar evolution.

The day’s main data paper is ALICE asking how low in multiplicity partonic flow survives. A two-generator QED study also addresses the radiative corrections behind the BaBar ππ dispute.

Themes

Small systems, at the floor and at the nucleus

ALICE arXiv:2611.08327 finds baryon–meson v_2 splitting consistent with partonic collectivity in pp and p–Pb down to N_ch≥25. In the 15–25 bin the ratio keeps its shape, but significance drops to ~2σ (p–Pb) and <1σ (pp). After last week’s φ-flow result in O–O, this is the other end of the question: where the effect stops being measurable.

Duguet et al. arXiv:2611.08122 work from the nuclear side. Coupled-cluster emulators show that O and Ne quadrupole eccentricities respond linearly to all 16 N²LO chiral LECs, and that Ne–Ne mostly probes the spin-orbit force. The light-ion runs past oxygen become nuclear-force data, not just geometry inputs.

QED radiation, done twice

Delorme et al. arXiv:2611.07067 implement resummed QED corrections to e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) in both KKMC and SHERPA. The two agree to ≲0.04% at first order, and the paper adds a new rule for radiative return, where first-order corrections are O(1). That is the regime of BaBar’s ISR ππ result and its ~8×10⁻¹⁰ internal spread (11-04). One limit: the pions are still point-like scalars dressed with a form factor.

Two companion papers: - Abudinén et al. arXiv:2611.07366 add matrix-element-corrected QED antenna showers for hadron decays in Pythia+Vincia. - Gauld et al. arXiv:2611.08221 find EW corrections to neutrino CC DIS can exceed 10%. Above 10⁴ GeV, photon-initiated and coherent-W pieces contribute sizeably and are missing from POWHEG-BOX.

Neutrinos from far away

  • Bustamante et al. arXiv:2611.05170 use IceCube flavor composition to bound |U_τ4|²<0.88 at any sterile mass, projecting 0.12–0.14 by 2050.
  • Mondol et al. arXiv:2611.07013 are the first to combine JWST UV luminosity functions with Planck to constrain neutrino self-interactions. The limit is tighter than Planck alone.
  • Chevallier et al. arXiv:2611.08440 propose sub-GeV pion DM semi-annihilating to ν̅ to explain a “mild” Super-K ν̅_e excess, with JUNO as the test. This is presumably the 2.6σ DSNB indication from 10-27, though the abstract doesn’t say.

Top-philic, but which spin?

Lessa et al. arXiv:2611.08459 show a coloured scalar and a vector-like fermion match onto the same EFT operators. Only above-threshold p_T shapes separate them, and not easily. Banfi et al. arXiv:2611.08388 report NLO tt̅ with 2HDM scalar/pseudoscalar–QCD interference and full spin correlations in POWHEG. It is a status report, but it is the tool the toponium-vs-CP-odd-Higgs question needs.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.07578: A clean no-go aimed at a live hint. The anomaly-free escape route fails too, through contact interactions or relic-neutrino decoupling.
  • arXiv:2611.08327: The first systematic search for where partonic flow ends. The low bins are limited by uncertainty, not null.
  • arXiv:2611.07067: Two independent generators agreeing at 0.04%, for the process every ISR ππ measurement depends on.
  • arXiv:2611.08122: Light-ion flow as a chiral-EFT constraint, complementary to the binding energies and radii nuclear forces are usually calibrated on.
  • arXiv:2611.07826: A sampler that ignores its conditioner beats a trained MDN on 1D marginals. With CRPSS plus a k-NN information ceiling, both models turn out to be already at the limit.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.08043 Manifestation of scale symmetry in nuclear medium — Yong-Liang Ma (nucl-th). A second Mannque Rho memorial after Lee’s 10-27 memoir, built on the genuine-dilaton reading of Brown–Rho scaling.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.07864 Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering — Jorge Baeza-Ballesteros (for the Baryon Scattering Collaboration) et al. (hep-lat). Both power countings put deuteron unbinding near M_π≈220 MeV.
  • arXiv:2611.07011 Constraining the spectral gap of 2d CFTs just above c=1 — Nathan Benjamin et al. (hep-th). Integer degeneracies cut the gap bound from ≲0.5 to <0.041 at c-1=3×10⁻³.
  • arXiv:2611.07819 Data-quality monitoring of luminosity blocks with ATLAS Open Data… — Renjie Wang (hep-ex). A public DQM benchmark. Its best detector catches 43% of injected defects at 1% false positives.
  • arXiv:2611.08482 Hypersurface covariance in relativistic local equilibrium — You-yu Li et al. (nucl-th). Claims to resolve, in principle, the hypersurface-dependence dispute behind the Λ-polarization sign puzzles.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.07578 — Can cosmic neutrinos induce a cosmic birefringence signal? (Mario Reig)

The Kalb–Ramond completion of the neutrino-current operator j_μA_νF̃^μν is exactly dual to a massless axion. In that dual theory the signal fixes g_aγ/f_ℓ=1/Λ_² independently of the 2-form normalisation. The Yin–Komatsu fit (44⁺¹²_-7 TeV√(ξ_ν_e)) gives Λ_≃10 TeV. Because j^μ must be an SU(2)L singlet, the axion picks up an electron coupling with g_aγg_ae=(1-c_R)m_e/Λ*²≃5.3×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ for ξ_ν_e=0.05. The bounds then close every branch:

  • Left-handed current. ALPS II requires g_ae≳1.8×10⁻³. That shifts a_e by -2×10⁻⁸, against agreement at ∼10⁻¹². The product also exceeds the CAST helioscope bound by eleven orders of magnitude. Stellar trapping does not rescue it: trapped axions boost solar conductivity, and protection requires g_ae≳40.
  • Electron lepton number (c_R=1). This current is anomalous. Since ALPS II caps f_ℓ≲0.3 GeV, it predicts BR(Z→γφ)≳0.1, against L3’s 10⁻⁶.
  • Higgs-dressed currents. These give excessive W and h decays to φ.
  • Anomaly-free currents (e.g. B-L). These leave a contact term ≳5×10⁵G_F. LEP and neutrino scattering exclude it, and it would also give N_eff≈12. Alternatively the axion velocity is set once at asymmetry generation, and relic neutrinos play no role in the rotation.

Why it matters: any confirmed isotropic rotation should be read as a light photon-coupled axion, not as a measurement of the relic-neutrino asymmetry.

Caveats: the Stückelberg alternative is dismissed on EFT-validity grounds (breakdown at ~keV, below BBN) rather than excluded by data. The stellar-trapping treatment uses order-of-magnitude solar-core estimates.

arXiv:2611.08327 — Exploring the limit of partonic collectivity in small collision systems at the LHC (ALICE Collaboration)

ALICE extracts identified-hadron v_2(p_T) in Run 2 p–Pb (198M events) and pp (226M events) in multiplicity bins. The method combines TPC–FMD long-range correlations, a template fit, and a three-subevent construction. Baryon–meson splitting over 3<p_T<5 GeV/c:

N_ch bin p–Pb pp
≥50 6.13σ —
25–50 5.28σ 4.78σ
15–25 1.95σ 0.35σ

Mass ordering and the ~2.2 GeV/c crossing persist in every bin. In low-multiplicity p–Pb the baryon/meson ratios stay above unity past the crossing but return to unity at 4–6 GeV/c. In low-multiplicity pp, v_2(Λ)/v_2(K) sits below unity.

Why it matters: this is the first scan of where coalescence-type signatures fade. The ≥25 bins in pp now look like high-multiplicity p–Pb. In the 15–25 bin the authors explicitly decline to claim presence or absence of splitting, because uncertainties dominate. It complements last week’s O–O φ-flow result from the opposite direction: the floor rather than the reach.

Caveats: - The non-flow template baseline is N_ch<15, directly adjacent to the lowest signal bin. Baseline variation is already the dominant systematic (4% p–Pb, 7% pp). - Equal N_ch in pp and p–Pb need not mean equivalent physics. - Run 3 statistics are needed to settle the low bins.

arXiv:2611.07067 — QED corrections to e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) with amplitude-level resummation (Stéphane Delorme et al.)

Amplitude-level YFS resummation for π⁺π⁻⁽γ) is implemented independently in KKMC (CEEX) and SHERPA (ACRAIC). Both include exact one- and two-photon trees, the full one-loop correction with initial–final boxes, and the exact one-loop correction to single-photon emission. First-order fiducial cross sections agree to ≲0.04% across all five STRONG2020 scenarios. The second-order theory-nuisance bands are:

  • ~0.005% at CMD
  • ~0.1% at KLOE-I
  • ~0.02% at KLOE-II
  • ~0.4% at BESIII
  • ~0.9% in the 10 GeV B scenario, the setup matching BaBar’s ISR measurement

The new radiative-return parameter handles the regime where the first-order correction r_1 is O(1), up to order −1 at BESIII and B. It uses the last relative correction as its template and normalises it by the YFS exponent γ=2(α/π)(L-1). At O(α) it dominates the bands (~6% at BESIII, ~9% at B) and covers the −5% and −10% second-order steps. The exception is low M_ππ, where a second hard photon enters at leading order. There an explicit ππγ NLO calculation is needed; it agrees with BabaYaga@NLO to ~1%, and to ~0.1% around the ρ.

At KLOE-I both generators follow BabaYaga@NLO, not PHOKHARA, in the pion polar-angle shape. GVMD loops lower the CMD-3 charge asymmetry by up to 1.15×10⁻² near 0.78 GeV, so form-factor modelling dominates that observable.

Caveats: - Pions are point-like scalars with a factorised form factor, and vacuum polarisation is off throughout. - Two-loop boxes, the genuine two-loop pion vertex and O(α³) are missing. - The KLOE-I second-order steps differ by ~0.06%, several times the statistical error. - The radiative-return parameter underestimates the missing higher orders wherever real and virtual corrections cancel.

item.title: Thursday, November 5, 2026
item.description:
Chiral lattices and Tera-Z reach

Witten arXiv:2611.05051 describes a variant of Craig’s algorithm for 4D gauge theories with chiral fermions, a variant Hsu also proposed recently. The lattice gauge field is interpolated over the continuum and coupled to continuum chiral fermions. It works in any dimension and for any anomaly-free representation, but it cannot run as Monte Carlo, because the chiral fermion path integral is not positive. Most of the rest of the day is projections and readout hardware rather than data. The physics cluster is FCC-ee reach, picking up last week’s finding that Tera-Z precision decides minimal SU(5) at three loops. The hard numbers are older or limits: ATLAS’s 8 TeV diphoton+jets measurement and Auger’s sterile-neutrino bounds.

Themes

Chiral fermions, lattice and ladder

Witten’s note pairs with Chi et al. arXiv:2610.42103. They run DMRG on a four-leg ladder realization of the 3-4-5-0 chiral model and find quantized charge pumping in all three boundary phases, including a fully gapped symmetric-mass-generation edge. Their analogy to topological leptogenesis via B-L is suggestive rather than derived.

FCC-ee as the decisive test

Greljo et al. arXiv:2611.05464 put vector-like “flavour chain” messengers at the TeV scale. They then show the same Higgs couplings shift Z/W couplings at tree level: LEP/SLD already require M_F/|y_F|≳3 TeV, and FCC-ee would reach 100 TeV. Vignaroli arXiv:2611.05501 projects Z-pole reach for heavy-neutral-lepton dipoles. The reach matches HL-LHC at 1 TeV, though local UV operators can mimic all four coupling shifts. Lahiri et al. arXiv:2611.05685 target the CP phase of the 95 GeV scalar via ττ asymmetries at Higgs factories.

Haloscopes, readout first

Wu et al. arXiv:2611.05444 claim a 5–10× scan-rate gain over quantum-limited homodyne detection from electro-optic photon counting at 5–12 GHz. Their optimum uses an overcoupled cavity. Wiedemann et al. arXiv:2611.06761 cover the other end with a 300–700 MHz KI-TWPA at 2.5–3.5 quanta. Both continue the cavity-side work that followed last month’s off-haloscope proposals.

What the data actually pin down

Serao et al. arXiv:2611.06129 find that combined spectroscopy plus g-2 leaves formally unbounded X17 nucleon-coupling directions. That matters because yesterday’s FASER result left only the high-coupling window open. Serao also wrote yesterday’s Ge/Xe blind-direction paper, so identifiability is becoming a habit. Abbas et al. arXiv:2611.06824 show the four known Adler coefficients resolve c_5,1 only to about ±24, and that the often-quoted 283 is a linear extrapolation.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.05051: Witten on a decades-old obstruction. The algorithm works in principle; the sign problem is why it doesn’t work in practice.
  • arXiv:2611.05464: A naturalness-motivated flavour model with a sharp Tera-Z falsification target, reaching tunings of 10⁻⁴.
  • arXiv:2611.05432: Bondarenko et al. show Kharzeev–Levin parton entropy computed from densities is an upper bound, not entanglement, unless a subsystem is specified. They also give a Lindblad derivation of LO DGLAP and propose a test against HERA and LHC hadron multiplicities.
  • arXiv:2611.06769: Frederix et al. fix the shower starting scales that blocked a public release, so Born spreading is now in MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, including FxFx. Fewer negative weights, and W+jets samples generate 6× faster.
  • arXiv:2611.05469: Kim et al. use the qubit itself as the scattering target, opening eV–keV dark matter with a geometry-to-cross-section recipe.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.05453 The Search for the Top Quark — Paul D. Grannis (physics.hist-ph). Discovery history from a D0 insider.
  • arXiv:2611.05817 Hybrid Hadrons: Origins and Development — Eric S. Swanson (hep-ph). Careful priority-tracing with participants’ recollections.
  • arXiv:2611.06586 Operational Challenges in Efficient and Sustainable Operation of the Event Processing Nodes GPU Farm at the ALICE Experiment — Federico Ronchetti et al. (hep-ex). Running CERN’s largest GPU farm, 2800 GPUs at 50 kHz.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.05500 SMEFT Constraints on Top Electroweak Couplings and a Composite Higgs Interpretation — Leandro Da Rold et al. (hep-ph). A 46-coefficient fit that favors negative C_Hq⁽⁻⁾ and C_Ht, with a composite model to match.
  • arXiv:2611.05475 Complete set of bounded-from-below conditions for the A_4-symmetric three-Higgs-doublet model — Luís Lavoura et al. (hep-ph). Field ansätze devised with Claude, then checked against 10⁶ brute-force minimizations.
  • arXiv:2611.05465 Probing Heavier-Baryon Oscillations through Light-Baryon Mixing — Arnau Bas i Beneito et al. (hep-ph). Indirect Ξ_b,c⁰ bounds 3–5 orders stronger than direct limits, as order-of-magnitude estimates.
  • arXiv:2611.06755 Earthquake Forecast via Neutrino Tomography at the DUNE Baseline — Bipin Singh Koranga et al. (hep-ph). The authors’ own verdict: short-term forecasting is not feasible.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.05051 — A Note On Lattice Definition of Gauge Theories With Chiral Fermions (Edward Witten)

Witten defines a lattice chiral gauge theory without lattice fermions. The link variables are restricted to “admissible” fields, meaning every plaquette satisfies |U_P-1|<ϵ. Each admissible configuration is interpolated to a continuum gauge field, and continuum chiral fermions are coupled to that field. The fermion weight is |D̸_W⁺|exp(-iπη(𝒟_Y)), where η is the APS eta-invariant on a five-manifold Y bounding spacetime. By the Dai–Freed gluing law, this weight is independent of the choice of Y exactly when the representation is free of both perturbative and global anomalies. Instanton sectors are handled with fiducial cobordism generators. Their phases are the renormalized theta-angles. Infinite-order generators give continuous thetas, and torsion generators give discrete ones.

The construction works for any compact gauge group, any anomaly-free representation, any dimension, and any compact spin manifold, not just T⁴. Witten justifies the general-manifold case by the requirement that chiral theories couple consistently to gravity. He notes that on T⁴ the cluster-decomposition shortcut fails for discrete thetas and for fractional instanton number. He also argues that numerically evaluating the continuum determinant does not reintroduce doubling.

The caveats are explicit: - Sign problem. The chiral fermion weight is not positive, so the scheme cannot be run as Monte Carlo. - Admissibility. Irrelevance of the admissibility constraint in the continuum limit rests on the asymptotic-freedom expectation, not a proof. - Novelty. Witten describes the main novelty as “possibly” a sharper treatment of the fermion path integral and its anomalies. The same variant appears in Hsu, and earlier proposals ran along similar lines.

arXiv:2611.05464 — Flavour Chains at the TeV Edge (Admir Greljo et al.)

Vector-like-fermion chains generate Yukawas as y_F z^N with z≃0.02, and the Minimal Flavour Protection group SU(2)_q×U(1)_X protects them. The same Higgs link generates 𝒪_Hℓ,Hq⁽¹,3) at tree level with C∼|y_F|²/M_F² and no spurion suppression.

Current bounds - A six-class fit to LEP/SLD data, cross-checked with three public codes, gives M_F/|y_F|≳3–7 TeV. The indicative tuning is 1/Δ_total≃0.3%. - B_s→μμ is currently stronger for the down-type classes, at about 9 TeV. Projected flavour reach stays at about 9 TeV or below.

FCC-ee projections - The reach is about 100 TeV unprofiled and about 50 TeV profiled. - The profiled tuning reaches 𝒪(10⁻³⁾ in scenario S1 and 𝒪(10⁻⁴⁾ in S2. - In the experiment-only scenario, the profiled bounds collapse to a nearly universal 52–57 TeV. This reflects an approximate flat direction from the R_f ratios, which better Γ_Z precision could lift.

Why rearranging the chain doesn’t escape. Moving the Higgs link shifts the effect between left- and right-handed currents but fixes their product. The floor becomes M_F≳(|y_F| y Λ_LΛ_R)¹/2, which puts the b and τ chains above 15 and 10 TeV at Tera-Z. That configuration is about 100× less tuned than the minimal chain but still heavily tuned. This estimate assumes Λ_R≈Λ_L, which the authors did not compute.

Caveats - The tuning scales as |y_F|⁴, and |y_F|∼0.2 removes today’s tuning entirely. - The Higgs-criticality motivation needs |y_F|≳0.7. With 18 Higgs-coupled states, it lowers h_crit from 3×10¹¹ GeV to 7.3 TeV at the 5 TeV benchmark. - That mechanism still needs stabilizing bosons below about 100 TeV and leaves a 3×10⁻³ residual hierarchy.

arXiv:2611.05432 — Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution (S. Bondarenko et al.)

Entropy from densities. The one-parton matrix built from Lipatov’s wave functions supports two distinct entropies: - Sampled-parton entropy: S_1, computed from the trace-normalized matrix. - Mode entropy: S_mode=∑_λg_B(n_λ), which bounds any state with the same one-body data, S_vN≤S_mode. Equality holds only for the thermal Gaussian state.

The pure hadron has zero entropy regardless of its occupations. The Kharzeev–Levin geometric entropy is g_B(n̅-1), the one-mode special case. Its large-n̅ form 1+lnn̅ is 47% high at n̅=1.5.

Rapidity cells. Summing isolated unit-rapidity cell entropies, rather than merging them, overcounts by Δ_Y=12ωY². At ω=0.4 this is 11.6 at Y=8, a factor of 3.8. The gap depends on the chosen resolution.

Evolution. Averaging over unrecorded emission histories, assumed incoherent across scales, gives a Lindblad equation in lnQ² with Σ̂=ℛ̂^†ℛ̂/2. Its occupations reproduce LO DGLAP, including virtual terms, at leading-log accuracy. This holds for strong k_⊥ ordering in light-cone gauge with dilute occupations.

Caveats - The thermal-Gaussian closure supplies Bose/Pauli factors, but its own error estimate is unfavourable. Its initial rate derivative deviates from the exact one by a relative 4n and has the wrong sign for 1/6<n<1/2. - The Lamb-shift-like term is set to zero by assumption. - No recombination is derived. - The proposed HERA/LHC test compares mode numbers inferred from hadron factorial moments with transverse mode counts. The extracted text cuts off before the test is specified.

item.title: Wednesday, November 4, 2026
item.description:
BaBar’s ππ, measured twice

BaBar arXiv:2611.04596 re-measures e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) with the full 460 fb⁻¹ ISR sample. This time it separates pions from muons by their angular distributions rather than by particle ID. The new analysis alone gives a_μ^ππ=525.9±3.5±3.8 (×10⁻¹⁰, 0.3–1.4 GeV). Combined with the 2009 measurement it gives 517.8 ± 2.4 ± 3.3, so the earlier BaBar result must sit well below the new one. How the paper quantifies that compatibility is the section to read. It lands the day after another slice of the τ-route isospin budget for HVP was tightened (11-03). Elsewhere, toponium gets its first NNLO cross section, and FASER closes part of the X17 parameter space.

Themes

NRQCD at higher order

Klein et al. arXiv:2611.03782 compute the NNLO short-distance coefficient for pseudoscalar toponium and get 4.87 pb at 13 TeV. Scale uncertainties shrink roughly fourfold relative to NLO, but the Coulomb-scale dependence of the matrix elements now dominates the error. That makes the remaining uncertainty a bound-state problem, the same treatment Buccioni’s genus-two threshold expansions (10-26) still lacked. It is also the piece the NRQCD-vs-CP-odd-Higgs reading of the CMS excess turns on. Smaller NRQCD entries: Li et al. arXiv:2611.04910 find NLO more than doubles the T_4c radiative widths, and Gong et al. arXiv:2611.04981 argue that slow convergence in J/ψ+η_c is intrinsic to the process.

Old signals, closed windows

  • X17. FASER arXiv:2611.03904 recasts its dark-photon and ALP nulls as a protophobic X17 and excludes 6×10⁻⁵<ϵ_e<1.2×10⁻⁴. A high-coupling window remains, which matters given September’s finding that cosmic muons reproduce the Atomki opening-angle peaks.
  • DAMA. Heikinheimo et al. arXiv:2611.04890 add inelastic scattering, quenching variations and halo rescaling to the full NREFT. DAMA still cannot coexist with LZ, PICO-60 and CDMSlite.
  • Squarks. Agashe et al. arXiv:2611.03794 go the other way: the simplified model undercounts production, and the realistic LHC limit is 2.6–3.0 TeV.

Light ions, ordered by density

Neeraj et al. arXiv:2611.04865 show that the CMS O–O Λ/K⁰_S shape is not set by multiplicity. Matching p–Pb at equal transverse density cuts the mismatch by ~60%, and the tension disappears only with sub-nucleonic structure. Ambrus et al. arXiv:2611.05239 find Ne/O v_2 ratios are robust across hydro and kinetic theory, while v_3 ratios are not. Both extend last week’s push past oxygen toward Ne–Ne.

Weak mixing at low Q

Huang et al. arXiv:2611.03751 propagate PREX-II/CREX to neutron radii below 1% uncertainty and extract sin²θ_W=0.231⁺⁰.016_-0.015 from COHERENT. That sits between CONUS+’s 0.225 and the CEνNS+ν–e combination at 0.233. Serao et al. arXiv:2611.04600 warn that Ge and Xe targets leave nearly parallel blind directions for light mediators.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.04596: A new pion/muon separation and an internal BaBar spread of ~8×10⁻¹⁰. (Also posted as arXiv:2611.04621.)
  • arXiv:2611.03782: The cross section any toponium-vs-scalar fit now needs, with the error budget located in the Coulomb scale.
  • arXiv:2611.03904: A collider null that bites into the X17 parameter space directly, rather than a projection.
  • arXiv:2611.04865: Uses only published data, and gives a falsifiable Ne–Ne prediction (within 3–5% of O–O).
  • arXiv:2611.03794: Moves quoted squark limits by ~1 TeV. HL-LHC and FCC-hh reach estimates inherit the correction.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.04531 A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime — Aimé Matheron et al. (hep-ex). Colliding an XFEL with a high-intensity laser improves the low-energy bound by ten orders of magnitude.
  • arXiv:2611.03783 GUT Color-Triplet Around the Corner… — Gia Dvali et al. (hep-ph). Splits Yukawas instead of masses, giving a TeV-scale long-lived triplet. It is the opposite bet to the IR-fixed M_H_c behind Allwicher’s SU(5) flip (11-02).
  • arXiv:2611.04267 Semiparametric Estimation of Physics Parameters and Parton Distribution Functions — Huanbiao Zhu et al. (hep-ph). An influence-function debiasing removes the need for joint PDF+SMEFT refits, extending last week’s fit-machinery thread.
  • arXiv:2611.03813 Presupernovae Strongly Constrain Electrophilic MeV Bosons — Yu Cheng et al. (hep-ph). Progenitor-phase 511 keV injection beats supernova bounds by up to 100× at 1–3 MeV.
  • arXiv:2611.04014 Branching Fractions and CP-Violating Asymmetries in D => PP Decays — Franco Buccella et al. (hep-ph). Charged-mode tension persists. The paper gives testable K⁰_SK⁰_S and π⁰π⁰ asymmetry predictions for the still-open charm-CPV question.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.04596 — A New Precise Measurement of the e⁺e⁻→π⁺π⁻⁽γ) Cross Section with the ISR Method at BaBar (BaBar Collaboration)

The new analysis drops particle ID and separates ππγ from μμγ with template fits to |cosθ^| in bins of two-track mass. Pions follow sin²θ^; muons go from flat to 1+cos²θ^. This allows a p_T>0.1 GeV track cut instead of the 2009 analysis’s 1 GeV/c, which retains the asymmetric topologies at large |cosθ^| where the two shapes differ most. The fit uses 7.6M events from the full 460 fb⁻¹. As a validation, the muon spectrum is compared absolutely to QED and gives R_μμ=0.9920 with 0.69% total precision; the analysis was unblinded only after this check.

The result is a_μ^ππ(0.3–1.4 GeV)=525.9(3.5)(3.8), against 513.3(2.2)(3.1) for 2009. The gap is 12.6×10⁻¹⁰, and the new cross section sits ~2% higher across the ρ peak. Compatibility is assessed in two ways: - Local scan: in 50 MeV intervals the differences are mostly <2σ in the central region, and conservative systematic-correlation scenarios move these by ≤0.2σ. - Integrated window: over 0.6–0.8832 GeV the 2009 result is −1.4σ from 2026.

The 517.8(2.4)(3.3) combination inflates uncertainties wherever local χ²>1. In the same window, 2026 is +0.9σ from CMD-3, −4.2σ from KLOE and −3.0σ from BESIII. BaBar calls it consistent with τ-based estimates and recent lattice results.

Caveats: - Below 0.5 GeV and above 1 GeV the μμ background overwhelms the signal, and the new result is not competitive with 2009. The 0.3–0.5 GeV piece reads 60.7 vs 57.6. - The combination therefore mixes two methods whose relative weight depends on energy.

arXiv:2611.03782 — Toponium hadroproduction at next-to-next-to-leading order in NRQCD (Sven Yannick Klein et al.)

The new ingredient is the NNLO QCD short-distance coefficient for gg→η_t. It uses nested soft-collinear subtraction, two-loop amplitudes and a soft-improved matching scheme. The cross section also includes: - NLO EW corrections, - Θ_t channels, - v² and P-wave terms, - associated production, - NNLO+RG-improved perturbative LDMEs summed over radial states.

At 13 TeV the result is σ=4.87⁺⁰.63_-0.65 pb. NLO raises LO by 28% and NNLO lowers NLO by 5%. The NLO EW term is a flat −7%, driven by y_t² Higgs exchange. All other pieces are each below about 1%; only qq̅→γ^/Z^→Θ_t reaches ~1% below 10 TeV. The seven-point scale band narrows about fourfold relative to NLO, to ⁺⁰.5%_-3.0%. The paper warns that the small NNLO shift at μ=m_t is unrepresentative, since the correction grows above 2m_t.

The error budget is now dominated by non-hard sources: - Coulomb scale of the LDMEs: ±12%, nearly independent of order and √(s). - α_s(m_Z): ±5%, also mainly through the LDMEs. - m_t: ±0.8%.

The authors point to N³LO S-wave LDMEs as the remedy; these already exist for the spin-triplet state.

Caveat: this is a zero-width result, counting only M_tt̅<2m_t. It is not yet the threshold spectrum ATLAS/CMS measure; that comparison awaits the promised finite-width Green’s-function extension.

arXiv:2611.03904 — Constraints on a Long-Lived X17 Vector Boson with FASER (FASER Collaboration et al.)

FASER statistically combines two existing searches: - Dark-photon search: 27 fb⁻¹, 0 events observed on a background of 2.3×10⁻³. - ALP search: 57.7 fb⁻¹, 1 event on 0.44±0.39. It uses the timing scintillator as a veto, so it covers decays after the decay volume and is orthogonal to the dark-photon search.

Together they use the full magnetized region as decay volume. The reinterpretation is for a strictly protophobic vector with ϵ_n=10⁻².

Production is dominated by proton bremsstrahlung, which is not suppressed despite ϵ_p=0. The form factors are evaluated at t=m_X², where both F_1 and F_2 are nonzero even though F_1(0)=0. η→Xγ and neutron bremsstrahlung at the TAN are subleading.

At 17 MeV the 90% CL CLs exclusion is 2×10⁻⁸<ϵ_e<3×10⁻⁴. That fully covers the low-coupling window 6×10⁻⁵–1.2×10⁻⁴, which had only recently reopened after an E141 re-analysis. The high-coupling window (6×10⁻⁴–1.5×10⁻³) survives because the X decays before reaching FASER. Under an alternative model with ϵ_n=ϵ_e, the excluded range is 2×10⁻⁵<ϵ<1.5×10⁻⁴.

Caveats: - The bremsstrahlung off-shell damping factor alone carries ~40% signal uncertainty. - The model is simplified: the small proton and axial couplings required by pion and kaon decay bounds are neglected. - Results are stated to be insensitive to ϵ_n within the Be-favoured range.

(Full texts for arXiv:2611.04865 and arXiv:2611.03794 were not supplied, so no deep dive is given for them here.)

item.title: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
item.description:
Upgrade I’s first rare-decay result

LHCb arXiv:2611.00230 uses 18 fb⁻¹ of 2024–25 data from the upgraded detector for three results:

  • the first single-experiment evidence for B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻;
  • the world’s most precise B_s⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ branching fraction;
  • the most precise B_s⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ effective lifetime.

All three agree with the SM, alone and combined with Runs 1–2. That fits the season’s split in flavor. The cleanest exclusive channels keep landing on the SM, while the live tensions sit in C_9 and |V_cb|. The abstract gives no numbers, so open the paper to see how far Run 3 moves things. CMS adds a |V_cb| measured from top decays. The rest of the day’s weight is in FPGA-budget ML and in whether predicted phase transitions actually complete.

Themes

|V_cb| without hadronic inputs

CMS arXiv:2611.01274 extracts |V_cb|=(4.59⁺⁰.44_-0.48⁺⁰.64_-0.76)×10⁻² from W→cb in tt̅. It is free of the nonperturbative inputs behind the inclusive/exclusive split, which is what that puzzle needs. At roughly 19% uncertainty, though, it can’t settle it yet. Esparza Arellano et al. arXiv:2611.01683 tighten the ωπ correction to τ→ππνγ. That shrinks another piece of the τ-route isospin-breaking budget for HVP, after Bashir et al.’s ρππ term on 10-21.

Transformers in 147 ns

  • SCRAMJet. Sharma et al. arXiv:2611.00086 reach 71.4% JetClass accuracy on a VU13P. That is 6.1 points above the best resource-constrained model, using an eighth of the operations.
  • SpikePID. Tsoi et al. arXiv:2611.00104 beat an 8.6× larger MLP on K/π cluster counting with a 529-parameter spiking network.
  • Localized anomalies. Mendiratta et al. arXiv:2611.00234 show a calorimeter flow’s global likelihood misses localized signals that a regional latent score catches.

After LEAF (10-21) through CoReNet yesterday, the open question is what survives quantization, not whether models can shrink.

Which transitions finish

Chiang arXiv:2611.01634 studies the type-II seesaw. The usual v_c/T_c>1 criterion flags degeneracies that never complete. The transitions that do complete are weak, sphaleron-unsafe and far below LISA, and they depend strongly on the RG scale. Araújo et al. arXiv:2610.40354 find genuine two-peak spectra in two-field conformal models. This continues yesterday’s idealization-dropping GW papers: a GW forecast is only as good as its transition dynamics.

Agents, with receipts

Gao et al. arXiv:2611.03373 have an agent reproduce a CEPC Bell-observable analysis to ~2% without being given the published numbers as targets. It then traces the detector-level shift mainly to muon isolation. Zhao’s CELEBI arXiv:2611.01788 pins each result to an immutable analysis state. After QFT-Bench showed correct answers with unfaithful reasoning (10-27), provenance is the right thing to build.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2611.00230: The first rare-decay physics from Upgrade I. Check how much the B⁰/B_s ratio tightens.
  • arXiv:2611.01158: Roy et al. give the 248 keV LZ event an exothermic Higgs-portal relic. It needs no high-velocity tail, the input Zhang et al.’s Gaia reconstruction undercut on 10-22, and solar-capture annihilation is suppressed. It predicts a sub-MeV photon continuum for COSI. It is the first model for the event after two blank days.
  • arXiv:2611.00086: “Virtual channels”: quantization-aware training drops attention channels from the compiled circuit while they still carry signal in training, so the loss never sees them go. A datalane floor recovers 3.1 points. Required reading for anyone using HGQ-style training.
  • arXiv:2611.00141: Kühler et al. give the full one-loop SM in BMHV with all symmetry-restoring counterterms. QCD always contributes to the breaking, so the SM must be treated as a whole. This is groundwork for multi-loop EW precision, the precision that flipped minimal SU(5) yesterday.
  • arXiv:2611.01285: CMS’s first charm dead-cone study in PbPb. Medium-induced radiation does not appear to fill the dead cone.

From the community

  • arXiv:2611.00239 From High Energy Astrophysical Neutrinos to the Nobel… — Maibam Ricky Devi (hep-ph). A tribute history from AMANDA to IceCube and Halzen’s 2026 Nobel.
  • arXiv:2611.03315 The search for the Higgs Boson and the EBH mechanism — John Ellis (physics.hist-ph). LEP and Tevatron Higgs searches, 1980–2000, from someone who was there.
  • arXiv:2611.01117 LHμC Concept… — Arda Goroglu et al. (hep-ex). The full concept for μ⁺p collisions at 5.3 TeV, following Piotrzkowski’s 10-27 pitch.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2611.00205 Lightest and heaviest nuclei as keys to the origin of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays — Anna M. Suliga et al. (astro-ph.HE). The authors claim Auger data confirm two predicted light-nucleus populations at ≥7.2σ and call this strong evidence for neutron-star-merger origins. Large claims; read the model dependence.
  • arXiv:2611.02559 Thermal Festina Lente — Fayez Abu-Ajamieh et al. (hep-th). With gauged B-L and Dirac neutrinos, the lightest neutrino must exceed 10–43 meV, in tension with DESI DR2 for most of that coupling range. Awkward next to the persistent negative-∑m_ν preference.
  • arXiv:2611.03407 Non-Global and Super-Leading Logarithms in Higgs Production through Vector Boson Fusion — Thomas Becher et al. (hep-ph). The first combined phenomenological study of both effects in the VBF gap veto.

Deep dives

arXiv:2611.00230 — Evidence for the decay B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ and improved measurements of the decay B⁰_s→μ⁺μ⁻ (LHCb collaboration et al.)

With 18 fb⁻¹ of 2024–25 Upgrade I data, LHCb sees a B⁰→μ⁺μ⁻ excess at 3.0σ, with ℬ=(1.26⁺⁰.51_-0.47⁺⁰.06_-0.05)×10⁻¹⁰. Combined with Runs 1–2, this becomes (1.14⁺⁰.42_-0.39⁺⁰.06_-0.05)×10⁻¹⁰ at 3.2σ. The SM predicts (1.03±0.05)×10⁻¹⁰, and the prior limit was <1.6×10⁻¹⁰ at 90% CL.

For B_s⁰, Run 3 alone gives (3.31⁺⁰.31+0.15_-0.30-0.13)×10⁻⁹. The combined fit gives (3.25⁺⁰.26+0.13_-0.25-0.12)×10⁻⁹, sitting somewhat below the SM’s 3.66±0.14.

On the digest’s question: the ratio is now measured rather than bounded, but loosely. The combined result is ℛ_μμ=0.035⁺⁰.014_-0.012, against 0.0280±0.0016 in the SM and in any MFV theory. At ~40% precision, that is not yet a meaningful test of non-CKM flavour structure.

The effective lifetime is 1.42±0.18±0.02 ps from Run 3 and 1.60±0.16±0.01 ps combined. Both are still statistically dominated, and 𝒜_ΔΓ_s^μμ=0.91±1.92 is unconstrained within its physical range.

Caveats visible in the paper: - The B_s branching fraction assumes 𝒜_ΔΓ_s^μμ=+1. Using −1 instead raises it by 9.2%. - The dominant B_s systematic (3%) is f_s/f_d=0.247±0.008 at 13.6 TeV, taken from an LHCb paper still in preparation. - The B⁰ systematic (4%) comes from misID and semileptonic background modelling. - The B_s yields from the lifetime and branching-fraction fits agree only at the 1.7σ level.

arXiv:2611.01158 — Exothermic Higgs portal: from LUX-ZEPLIN recoil to Gamma Rays (Subhojit Roy et al.)

(Authors are Roy and Zupan.) The model is a complex singlet split into ϕ_1,2 by a few hundred keV, coupling only through an off-diagonal Higgs portal g ϕ_1ϕ_2 H^†H. The relic abundance fixes g and leaves r_2≃0.5 of the dark matter in the excited state today.

At the benchmark (m_ϕ_1=100 GeV, Δm=600 keV, g≃0.0515), the predictions are: - LZ rate: ϕ_2 A→ϕ_1 A down-scattering gives N_ϵ≃1.63 efficiency-weighted events in the 2.84 t·yr exposure. This uses the Standard Halo Model and needs no velocity tail. - Diphoton decay: ϕ_2→ϕ_1γγ has τ≃4.5×10²³ s, about 40× above a recast INTEGRAL/SPI bound. That recast neglects inter-bin correlations and template systematics. About 83% of the photons fall above COSI threshold. - Dwarf annihilation: ⟨σv⟩_equiv=2.26×10⁻²⁶ vs a Fermi-LAT limit of 3.34×10⁻²⁶ cm³/s. That is a thin margin, and the dwarfs exclude m_ϕ_1≲72 GeV. - Solar capture: capture leaves the Sun’s population mostly in ϕ_1. The resulting WW rate is ~10⁻¹³ of the IceCube limit. The captured-ϕ_1 × halo-ϕ_2 channel was not evaluated.

The main caveat is spectral. A xenon diffraction minimum near 270 keV pushes the predicted peak to ~180 keV. The model expects 1.18 events in 100–200 keV but only 0.22 in 215–270 keV, where the candidate sits. The total yield also depends strongly on nuclear modelling: 1.63 events with the default response, 4.70 with a Helm form factor, and 1.61 with chiral EFT. No event-level likelihood is performed.

arXiv:2611.00086 — SCRAMJet: An Ultra Low Latency JetClass-Scale Transformer for the HL-LHC Level-1 Trigger (Aadeesh Sharma et al.)

The model is a single-block transformer with rank-2 Linformer attention, D=16, and 64 constituents, trained with per-parameter learned fixed-point quantization. It reaches 71.43±0.62% accuracy on ten-class JetClass with 0.157M MACs. That is 6.1 points above PHAT-JeT at one-eighth the MACs. On a VU13P it meets timing at 147 ns (21 cycles) using 25.7% of LUTs, and the RTL is bit-exact over 1.3M outputs.

The transferable result is the “virtual channel” mechanism. The quantizer masks zero-width channels only at inference, so training sees them while the circuit does not. One checkpoint scores 72.32% in training mode but 65.2% at inference, and 72.35% with the mask disabled; the mask explains the whole gap. All 7,015 sub-zero-width parameters sit inside attention.

The fix is a floor on the activation-quantizer bit-widths; the inherited constraint only covered weight quantizers. At EBOPs matched to within 0.12%, the floor lifts accuracy from 66.38% to 69.48%.

Caveats: - That same floored design compiles to 42% more adder-graph units, so EBOPs can rank designs opposite to their real cost. Width cuts are the reliable lever: halving D removed 38.8% of compiled cost at no accuracy loss. - Macro AUC (0.9289) still trails PHAT-JeT by 0.010. - Results come from a 2M-jet training subset with three seeds.

(arXiv:2611.00141 and arXiv:2611.01285 were not supplied and are omitted.)

item.title: Monday, November 2, 2026
item.description:
Quad lenses lean toward core collapse

Gilman et al. arXiv:2610.40766 analyze 29 quadruply imaged quasars and find halo densities consistent with gravothermal core collapse. They interpret this as elastic Yukawa SIDM and apply cluster and satellite-evaporation limits. The favored region is 20–80 GeV dark matter with MeV mediators and σ/m∼10²–10⁴ cm²/g at 10 km/s. Mediator bounds then push them toward an invisibly decaying neutrinophilic scalar. This is the third result in two weeks pointing away from CDM-density subhalos. Zhang et al. found none of 5000+ CDM subhalos dense enough, and Tekverk et al. found SIDM matches three known perturbers far more often. The new paper is a population statement, not a per-perturber one, though the authors still say “hints.” Elsewhere, an extra loop order excludes a minimal SUSY GUT, and phase-transition GW predictions shed three idealizations. The 248 keV LZ event drew no papers.

Themes

Phase transitions, less idealized

Three papers each relax a standard assumption: - Cutrona et al. arXiv:2610.40775 find that gravity, through non-minimal couplings, can enlarge or shrink the parameter space where supercooled radiative-symmetry-breaking transitions complete. - Finetti et al. arXiv:2610.40781 let dark-sector sound waves leak into the visible fluid. The total GW signal is generally suppressed and its spectral shape changes. - Blum et al. arXiv:2610.41504 show nucleated bubbles are not spherical, with δR/R∼(ħ/S_b)¹/2≈0.1 for typical cosmological transitions.

This is in the spirit of last week’s error-budget thread, now applied to GW forecasts.

Loop order decides

Allwicher et al. arXiv:2610.40821 find that Tera-Z gauge-coupling precision becomes sensitive to higher-loop running all the way up. In minimal SU(5) with proton-decay limits, two loops point to PeV-scale SUSY, while three loops appear to exclude the model.

Adelaja et al. arXiv:2610.40823 propose a retained signature-changing soft-gluon term as the source of the unexplained non-planar ζ_2 violations at small x. Those violations appear in the three- and four-loop non-singlet splitting functions, which were September’s headline. The proposal reproduces both with no tuned coefficient and predicts five-loop terms.

Bera et al. arXiv:2610.42062 complete the leading-colour two-loop integrals for tt̅γ, including elliptic entries. That follows last week’s genus-two tt̅ amplitudes.

Structure over size

Alison et al.’s CoReNet arXiv:2610.40749 builds the decay chain into the architecture. With 1508 parameters it matches a transformer more than 100× larger in HH→4b, extending last week’s tagger-compression run. Hart et al.’s REM arXiv:2610.41889 goes from hits to particles to resonances in full simulation, beating ML particle flow. Chung arXiv:2610.41894 asks the information-theoretic version of the question for calorimeters.

Neutrino generators, rebuilt

Graham-Jones et al. arXiv:2610.40866 put a consistent chiral EFT with Δ(1232) pion production into Sherpa, going through FeynRules and UFO. Prasad et al. arXiv:2610.40912 decompose a DNN’s inclusive electron–carbon prediction into exclusive generator channels by reweighting.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.40766: A 29-lens population pointing at core collapse, with a concrete particle model attached. It is the strongest entry yet in the SIDM-vs-CDM lensing thread.
  • arXiv:2610.40821: The two-loop vs three-loop flip on minimal SUSY SU(5) is a sharp result. The “IR determination” of the colour-triplet mass explains why.
  • arXiv:2610.41894: Treats hadronic resolution as an information ladder. On the same Geant4 events, the full record reaches 1.29% vs 2.14% at 20 GeV, and each readout dimension gets a measured value.
  • arXiv:2610.40749: Already used in several CMS searches. It recovers truth jet pairings without ever being trained on them.
  • arXiv:2610.42143: Kats makes a first strange-quark polarimetry measurement via Λ in W→cs̅, on CMS Open Data. The result is consistent with zero for now; the method and projections are the point.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.40724 Nuclear-geometry-tagging events in high-energy Ne–Ne collisions — Joachim Carlo Kristian Bjerg Hansen et al. (nucl-th). In Glauber simulations, tip–tip ²⁰Ne configurations can be selected at ~0.55 purity, as the small-system program moves past oxygen.
  • arXiv:2610.40911 Search for long-lived heavy neutral leptons… — CMS Collaboration (hep-ex). Muon-system displaced vertices extend HNL reach to 2–4 GeV at mixings of 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁵. No excess.
  • arXiv:2610.40967 Separating Fermion and Gauge Resonances with Species-Dependent Lightcones in Warped Geometry — Lisa Randall et al. (hep-ph). Fermion partners at 6.6–12 TeV coexist with 30 TeV KK gluons.
  • arXiv:2610.40793 Layered Wire-Grid Haloscope for Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark Photons — Andrea Caputo (hep-ph). Projected axion reach below CAST up to 1.4 meV.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.40766 — Hints of self-interacting dark matter from strong gravitational lensing (Daniel Gilman et al.)

What they did. This is a recast, not new data. It takes the G26 likelihood on median core-collapse times in two halo-mass bins, 10⁶–10⁸ and 10⁸–10¹⁰.7 M_⊙, from 29 JWST quads. G26 disfavors CDM with Bayes factors of 8:1 to 24:1. The authors map that likelihood onto elastic Yukawa SIDM using the Gurian et al. gravothermal t_c, which is valid across Knudsen regimes.
