Both Hubble-motivated G-step benchmarks are disfavoured: ΔG/G_0=+0.04 at 73 Myr (EGSM) at 3.1σ, and +0.11 at 130 Myr (OGSM) at 4.0σ. The profile likelihood has its minimum at ΔG=0 for both transition times.

The mechanism is a radius memory in fully convective red dwarfs. Homology gives an equilibrium radius R∝G⁰.324, while the fast adiabatic response gives R∝G⁻¹. The perturbation then relaxes on t_relax≃0.05 t_KH∼10⁸ yr, which is comparable to the proposed look-back times. A drop from larger G therefore leaves today’s stars inflated.

The analysis uses: - MESA tracks with an implemented G-step; - a per-star starspot covering fraction treated as a nuisance parameter; - eight CHEOPS detached-eclipsing-binary M dwarfs (0.1–0.31 M_⊙, periods ≥5 d) with mass–radius correlations ρ=0.53–0.90.

This gives Δχ²⁼⁹.52 (EGSM) and 16.41 (OGSM). Because the spot fractions sit at their physical boundary, the significances come from a parametric bootstrap rather than Wilks’ theorem.

The test is independent of the disputed solar and terrestrial modelling arguments.

Caveats: - Boundary stars drive the result. All of the leverage comes from the four stars pinned at f_spot=0, where spots can no longer absorb the extra inflation. - One star dominates. Dropping J2343+29 cuts the significances to 2.45σ (EGSM) and 1.90σ (OGSM). - Model systematics matter. A coherent 1% downward shift of the model radii lowers Δχ² to 5.72 and 10.92. - Only positive steps are tested. Both benchmarks have ΔG>0.

arXiv:2610.04557 — Violation and Restoration of Probability Positivity in Perturbative QFT (Bin Gong et al.)

The central argument concerns exclusive processes with colourless and neutral external states. There, each renormalized loop amplitude is IR-finite on its own and no KLN sum over unresolved states is needed. Gong et al. conclude that truncating the squared amplitude is an inherited QED habit, and that |∑_l≤M𝒜⁽l)|² is the right observable.

They recast eleven published NNLO results in the form Γ=Γ_LO|1+a_s(c_1+ic_2)+a_s²⁽c_3+ic_4)|². In every case both complex coefficients have modulus below 1, with the largest, 0.67, for J/ψ+η_c. Selected ratios Γ/Γ_LO at NLO, NNLO:

Channel Amplitude-level Squared-level
J/ψ→3γ 0.276, 0.126 −0.02, −0.44
Υ→3γ 0.426, 0.190 0.28, −0.11
e⁺e⁻→J/ψJ/ψ 0.40, 0.058 0.26, −0.38

J/ψ→3γ goes negative at NLO in the traditional expansion. Υ→3γ and double-J/ψ go negative at NNLO. Zhan et al. apply the same prescription to ultraperipheral J/ψ+γ.

Caveats, visible in the paper itself: - Partial higher orders. The NLO square keeps |ℳ_1|² but not the same-order 2Re(ℳ_0^*ℳ_2), so it contains incomplete 𝒪(α_s²⁾ terms. - Convergence is judged inside the modulus. The rates themselves still fall sharply from NLO to NNLO: by a factor 2.2 for J/ψ→3γ and about 7 for double J/ψ. - Positivity is not accuracy. Positivity is guaranteed by construction, which does not show the result is closer to the true value. - Mostly a reframing. The numbers re-express the group’s own earlier calculations, with α_s re-chosen for the B-factory channels.

arXiv:2610.04309 — Angular Observables in the Λ_b→Λνν̅ Decay (Wolfgang Altmannshofer et al.)

The full cascade Λ_b→Λ(→pπ⁻⁾νν̅ is described by five angular coefficients, S_1–4 and A_5; all but S_1 need Λ_b polarization. Z-pole Λ_b supply it: LEP measured 𝒫=-0.40±0.14.

The coefficients split by what they probe: - Chirality: S_1 and S_2 go as |C_R|²⁻|C_L|², which the mesonic modes cannot see. - CP phase: A_5 is a T-odd CP asymmetry proportional to Im(C_LC_R^*), with no flavour tagging or time dependence needed.

Mesonic data fix only |C_L±C_R|, so they confine the couplings to a ring via (|C_R|²⁻|C_L|²⁾²⁺⁴⁽Im C_LC_R^*)²⁼|C_R+C_L|²|C_R-C_L|². The baryonic observables pick the point on that ring.

SM predictions: - branching ratio (7.59±1.03)×10⁻⁶, dominated by form-factor and CKM uncertainties; - ⟨S_1⟩=-0.926±0.018; - an S_2 zero crossing at 12.6±1.2 GeV² that is independent of the Wilson coefficients, and so tests the form factors.

Projected FCC-ee reach, assuming a 10% branching-ratio measurement: - Real couplings: S_1 and S_2 break the four-fold real-coupling degeneracy even at ±0.5 uncertainty on the angular observables. - Complex couplings: at ±0.1 all four benchmarks are distinguishable from the SM. At ±0.5 the A_5 sensitivity is largely lost and only the pure right-handed benchmark survives.

This bears directly on the Belle II K⁺νν̅ excess, which the authors put about 2.7σ above the SM.

Caveats: - No dedicated angular estimates. The ±0.1–0.5 uncertainties are assumed scans. - Simplified meson comparison. The mesonic side is a 5% toy estimate. - Only right-handed currents show up. A pure rescaling of C_L leaves every angular observable unchanged. - Dark-sector explanations not covered. Light invisible states are explicitly excluded, although several Belle II interpretations rely on them.

item.title: Monday, October 5, 2026
item.description:
Jet vetoes reach third order

The jet-vetoed Higgs cross section now has a full third-order prediction. Abreu et al. pair a three-loop rapidity anomalous dimension arXiv:2610.03472 with N³LO+N³LL jet-vetoed Higgs arXiv:2610.03687, landing at ~3% residual uncertainty for p_T^v∼30 GeV. Last Wednesday the same observable got its first NLL non-global treatment (Becher et al.), so this process has advanced on two fronts in a week. Super-K’s first reactor-antineutrino observation is the day’s experimental headline. On LZ, a single paper appeared, and it reads like a consolidation of the heavy-Higgsino escape route.

Themes

Jet vetoes at third order

Abreu et al. arXiv:2610.03472 extract the anomalous dimension from a three-loop SCET soft function for generalized-k_t clustering as a function of R. The semi-numerical method is offered as reusable for other three-loop soft functions. The phenomenology companion arXiv:2610.03687 finds resummation lifts the fixed-order result by ~3%. Fiore et al. arXiv:2610.02327 add the first fully differential NNLO photon+identified-hadron predictions, aimed at FF fits and as a pp baseline for photon-tagged heavy-ion studies.

First light for neutrinos and muons

Super-K arXiv:2610.03143 sees reactor ν̅e at ~6σ in SK-Gd. Its reactor-only Δm²_21=(9.08⁺⁰.55-0.54)×10⁻⁵ eV² sits about 3σ above JUNO’s value from last week, though sin²θ_12=0.50±0.16 shows how little this sample constrains yet. COMET arXiv:2610.02855 reports Phase-α, the first demonstration of low-momentum μ⁻ transport through its solenoid. Measured yields run ~30% above Geant4.

Quantum structure, collider to plasma

Bao et al. arXiv:2610.03024 give a full-detector STCF study of ττ concurrence at ~2% precision with 1 ab⁻¹, which extends the season’s tau-polarimetry thread to the detector level. Brambilla et al. arXiv:2610.02313 track Wigner negativity of bottomonium in the QGP and find that it plateaus near the 1S value. The mechanism is conditional purification: the medium dissolves the large-⟨r²⟩ modes, leaving the surviving ensemble close to 1S.

LLM and GPU tooling

Schwartz’s BootLoops arXiv:2610.02286 packages IBP reduction, differential equations, PSLQ and ball arithmetic for any agentic LLM to operate. This continues last week’s LLMs-inside-calculations cluster and points it outward to genomics and statistics. Sule arXiv:2610.02318 puts cluster hadronisation into GAPS, generating 10⁶ hadron-level events in ~4 s on a V100. Samuel et al. arXiv:2610.03339 treat track fitting as translation, and their model matches RANSAC.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.03687: The first third-logarithmic-order jet-vetoed Higgs prediction at ~3% uncertainty, likely the new reference for HL-LHC Higgs measurements.
  • arXiv:2610.03143: Super-K observes reactor antineutrinos for the first time. Its Δm²_21 is high relative to JUNO and only 1.9σ from SK’s own solar data, a small new handle on the solar–reactor question.
  • arXiv:2610.03692: Freese et al. fold in the LMC tail, the LZ sideband and four IceCube cooling variants. The thermal 1.1 TeV Higgsino survives only marginally; 2 TeV to hundreds of TeV at δ≈350–525 keV is comfortable. They also flag that the solar bound itself depends on poorly known elastic Higgsino–nucleon scattering.
  • arXiv:2610.02286: A deliberate attempt to make multi-loop bootstrap machinery an LLM-operable public utility.
  • arXiv:2610.02313: A clean quantitative statement that classicalization in open-quantum-system quarkonium is partial and depends on the observable. This matters for anyone using Langevin approximations.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.02667 Distinguishing the origin of cosmic birefringence: dark energy, dark matter, and neutrino asymmetry — Lu Yin et al. (astro-ph.CO). The low-ℓ EB shape separates axion dark energy from dark matter or neutrino-asymmetry sources. This is relevant to the year’s open birefringence question.
  • arXiv:2610.03455 Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Constraint on B-mesogenesis — James M. Cline et al. (hep-ph). Requires T_rh≳10 MeV for M_Φ≲100 GeV. It is another entry in BBN-as-referee for late baryogenesis.
  • arXiv:2610.02590 Multi-Band Constraints on Cosmic Strings: Unifying Harmonic and Burst Spectra — Hansong Zhang et al. (gr-qc). LVK bounds rule out three of four loop models as the source of the PTA signal.
  • arXiv:2610.03489 Search for pair-produced vector-like top quarks decaying into Lorentz-boosted top quarks and scalar bosons… — CMS Collaboration (hep-ex). Finds a 2.7σ local excess, 1.5σ global. Noted for completeness, not excitement.
  • arXiv:2610.03603 Electroweak Transitions of Hyperons and Charmed Baryons: Opportunities and Prospects — Patrik Adlarson et al. (hep-ph). A useful map that flags the emerging lattice-versus-experiment Ξ_c→Ξ semileptonic puzzle.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.03687 — Third-Order Logarithmic Resummation for Jet-Vetoed Higgs Production (Samuel Abreu et al.)

The first N³LL+N³LO prediction for the gluon-fusion zero-jet cross section gives 30.11 (+3.2%/−3.0%) pb at p_T^v=30 GeV, with R=0.4 anti-k_t jets at 13.6 TeV. That is ~3% above fixed-order N³LO (29.24 pb). The shift lies outside N³LO’s narrow +0.7/−2.2% scale band, so fixed-order scale variation alone misses the logarithmic correction. Relative to NNLL+NNLO, the central value rises ~4% and the uncertainty shrinks from 6–8% to ~3%. The new ingredient is the three-loop, algorithm-dependent rapidity anomalous dimension γ_ν⁽³⁾⁽R²⁾ from the companion paper, combined with the four-loop cusp, three-loop γ_V and two-loop boundary terms, all implemented in RadISH. The authors tested the expansion against NNLOJet H+jet with M=1 TeV and R=0.1. With Δγ_ν⁽³⁾ set to zero, the expansion visibly fails to converge, so the three-loop clustering term is numerically essential.

The physics point is that the previous NNLL+N³LO result had an accidental cancellation near 30 GeV. N³LL lifts it and restores a uniform 3–4% third-order correction for p_T^v≳20 GeV. Alternative matching schemes and log-switching prescriptions all agree within the band. The code is public (JetVHeto).

Caveats: - Missing effects: top and bottom mass effects and small-R resummation are not included. Both were 1–2% in earlier work, comparable to the quoted uncertainty. - ln R terms: the authors flag large subleading lnR terms in γ_ν⁽³⁾ as motivation for lnR resummation. - Factorization breaking: coherence-violating effects, which break factorization from five loops, are explicitly set aside. The non-global/super-leading front noted in the digest therefore sits outside this calculation.

arXiv:2610.03143 — First observation of electron antineutrinos from nuclear reactors at Super-Kamiokande (K. Abe (The Super-Kamiokande Collaboration) et al.)

SK-Gd sees reactor ν̅_e via IBD with Gd-tagged neutrons. The exposure is 411.52 live days: SK-VI at 0.011% Gd and SK-VII at 0.033% Gd. The no-reactor hypothesis gives Δχ²⁼³⁴.7, about 6σ, and the oscillated fit has χ²⁼¹⁶.7/16.

Reactor-only fit, with θ_13 fixed: - sin²θ_12=0.500±0.155 - Δm²_21=(9.08⁺⁰.55_-0.54)×10⁻⁵ eV²

Comparison with SK solar. SK’s own solar fit gives Δm²_21=(6.10⁺¹.26_-0.86)×10⁻⁵ eV². The differences are 1.1σ in θ_12 and 2.2σ in Δm²_21. A parameter-goodness-of-fit test gives 1.9σ compatibility. The main text quotes Δχ²_PG=7.25 (p=0.027) while the appendix quotes 7.64 (p=0.022), a minor internal inconsistency. The combined SK fit is sin²θ_12=0.332, Δm²_21=(8.94⁺⁰.46_-0.47)×10⁻⁵ eV².

Why it matters: this is a new water-Cherenkov reactor handle on the solar sector, from the same detector that measures solar neutrinos. That makes it an internal CPT-motivated cross-check, and a demonstration of Gd-water for low-energy ν̅_e.

The paper does not quantify the digest’s “~3σ above JUNO” framing. It calls its values consistent with global fits and recent reactor results, JUNO included.

Caveats: - Background model: the accidental background comes from a single low-reactor window (Nov–Dec 2020) and is statistics-limited. - Flux inputs: fluxes use electrical rather than thermal load factors. - Systematics: neutron-capture γ modeling (5.4%) and coincidence efficiency (5.5%) dominate the listed systematics.

arXiv:2610.03692 — Higgsino dark matter compatible with the LZ high-energy nuclear-recoil event and IceCube constraints (Katherine Freese et al.)

Heavy Higgsinos can explain the 248 keV LZ event without violating IceCube solar bounds, but the thermal 1.1 TeV case barely survives. The authors build a 96-bin approximate LZ likelihood digitized from LZ’s published data, calibrated with 30k toys, which reproduces LZ’s interval near δ=350 keV. They include the corrected (4× larger) inelastic cross section.

Thermal 1.1 TeV case. The LZ-compatible splitting depends on the halo model: - SHM: 360–370 keV. - SHM+LMC: 485–505 keV.

IceCube lower bounds on δ at 1.1 TeV depend on how captured Higgsinos cool in the Sun:

Cooling assumption Lower bound on δ
Capture–annihilation equilibrium imposed 566 keV
Inelastic + elastic SD 558 keV
Inelastic only 506 keV

The thermal Higgsino survives only at δ≈508 keV, and only under three conditions together: LMC tail included, all elastic cooling neglected, and the LZ sideband dropped. The authors call this a limiting case rather than a robust interpretation.

Heavier Higgsinos. The key novelty is the m_χ⁻² falloff of the elastic SD cross section, which weakens cooling at high mass. With it, compatible regions open at: - ~2 TeV (δ~520 keV) for SHM+LMC, no sideband and SD-only elastic cooling. - ≳10–30 TeV (δ≈350–400 keV) for the SHM. - Equilibrium imposed everywhere: ≳80 TeV for the SHM, and 13–120 TeV (465–520 keV) for SHM+LMC.

They also find Sommerfeld resonances near 6.5, 25 and 55 TeV that locally tighten the bounds.

Caveats: - Halo model: the LMC tail uses a single simulated halo with a large LMC/MW mass ratio (0.27). - Sideband acceptance: unpublished, and LZ has not calibrated its nuclear-recoil response there. - Solar treatment: cooling assumes stationary nuclei, radial orbits and a uniform-density population. - IceCube conversion: the W⁺W⁻ limits are frozen above 10 TeV, so high-mass regions are extrapolations. - Cosmology: heavier Higgsinos need a non-standard abundance history.

item.title: Friday, October 2, 2026
item.description:
Fractional determinants, two uses

Pisarski arXiv:2610.00472 proposes that below T_χ the topological charge is fractional in units of 1/N_c. Fractional powers of Φ then enter the chiral Lagrangian. The consequence is a chiral transition that is generically second order, with exceptions at N_f=1 and N_f=3, and the prediction is testable with 2+1 lattice data. Giacosa et al. apply the same device to glueball decays the same day. The rest of the day is spread thin: LZ falls to three papers, all at high mass scales, and Drell-Yan gets a lattice-fed precision upgrade. A second paper in three days also argues against Dark Dimension graviton phenomenology.

Themes

Anomalies and glueballs

Giacosa et al. arXiv:2610.00484 couple a pseudoscalar glueball to fractional determinants. The model describes all four three-pseudoscalar channels of BESIII’s X(2370), and ηηη and ηηη’ rates would test it. That reading contrasts with Wednesday’s ϕh_1(1380) molecular interpretation. Issifu et al. arXiv:2610.01988 predict a parameter-free scalar-glueball radius of 0.28 fm, against a lattice value of 0.263(31) fm.

LZ: the survivors go heavy

Hor et al. arXiv:2610.01613 take the solar-capture escape at ∼10⁵ GeV Higgsinos seriously as SUSY SU(5). With GUT thresholds the model survives dimension-six proton decay, and p→K⁺ν̅ lands in Hyper-K/JUNO/DUNE reach. Khan et al. arXiv:2610.00226 concede that the LZ-matching part of their GmSUGRA Higgsino branch is disfavored by solar capture. Choudhury et al. arXiv:2610.00645 fit 0.2–1 TeV with a single dim-6 operator, but the abstract does not address the Sun.

Precision QCD, with lattice inputs

Assi et al. arXiv:2610.02169 reach N³LO+approx. N⁴LL′ Drell-Yan at particle level, using a continuum-lattice Collins-Soper kernel and strictly positive weights from maximum entropy. Last week’s negative-weight work tackled the same weights problem with optimal transport. Bertone et al. arXiv:2610.02096 argue that 𝒪(v²⁾ NRQCD describes J/ψ cross sections and polarization to P_T=360 GeV. Li et al. arXiv:2610.01154 fix IBP reductions from analyticity with only a few samples.

Streaming, tokens, retrieval

Xiotidis et al.’s A-GHOST arXiv:2610.01761 streams trigger-level data at 40–100 Gbps into GPU inference, with 0.118 ms p95 latency over hours without drops. Godi et al. arXiv:2610.00569 study scaling for residual-quantized full-event generation and find that token loss predicts physical fidelity. Kumar et al. arXiv:2610.00891 release an open RAG pipeline over about 230K papers, which extends this week’s LLM-in-the-loop thread.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.00472: A “beyond Landau” claim about the chiral transition, with a concrete lattice check proposed. It is likely to be argued over.
  • arXiv:2610.02169: Lattice nonperturbative input and positive-weight events in one Drell-Yan prediction. It is a candidate reference for m_W-type work.
  • arXiv:2610.01825: Langhoff shows that near-threshold KK decays are d-wave (Γ∝p⁵), which excludes flat-dark-dimension graviton DM. With Lee et al. on Wednesday, two independent hits on that program in three days.
  • arXiv:2610.01613: The LZ heavy-Higgsino escape route turned into a proton-decay prediction, which makes it the most testable LZ paper today.
  • arXiv:2610.01761: A working FPGA-to-GPU scouting architecture, not just a concept.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.00995 Search for dark matter produced in association with a low-multiplicity jet… — CMS Collaboration (hep-ex). The first LHC use of this signature; no excess.
  • arXiv:2610.01308 Search for charged-lepton-flavour violating eμtq interactions… — ATLAS Collaboration (hep-ex). Reports limits on six Wilson coefficients, with EFT again as the reporting language.
  • arXiv:2610.00460 ALP-Mediated Dark Matter at Low Reheating Temperature and the Belle II Excess — Joel Jones-Pérez et al. (hep-ph). The new mass-differential data leave the standard-cosmology Kνν̅ reading marginal.
  • arXiv:2610.00461 The Great Wall of the Standard Model — Yang Bai et al. (hep-ph). Domain walls could carry information about the SM’s global gauge-group quotient.
  • arXiv:2610.01289 Hadronization into Nuclei: Does Size Matter? — Anton Andronic et al. (nucl-th). The answer is no. That favors compact multi-quark formation for light (hyper)nuclei.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.00472 — Fractional anomalous determinants and the chiral phase transition (Robert D. Pisarski)

Pisarski proposes a “syncretic” chiral Lagrangian whose anomalous sector changes across T_χ. Below T_χ, topological charge is taken to be fractional in units of 1/N_c, so terms ℱ_j(Φ^†Φ) [(Φ)^j/N_c+h.c.] appear. The prefactors are fractional powers of Φ^†Φ, chosen so that each term behaves like Φ² as Φ→0. Above T_χ, only integer powers survive. The argument rests on assuming that in the Veneziano limit the free energy depends on θ/N_c. This yields a Witten–Veneziano generalization to arbitrary N_f/N_c in which the η’ stays massive at T_χ without a large ξ_1Φ. The predicted transition order by flavor number: - N_f=1: crossover (Z(2)-like). - N_f=2: second order, O(4). - N_f=3: still first order because the cubic Φ remains, but possibly very weakly so, since ξ_1 can be small. - N_f=4: a 𝒬=2/3 term could induce a weak, Halperin–Lubensky–Ma-type first-order transition.

The model is motivated by lattice data that find no first-order signal for N_f=3. One example is Zhang et al.’s susceptibility scaling exponent α≈0.39±0.04, which fits neither first order (α=3) nor Z(2) (α≈1.96). Another is the measured b_2≈-0.19/N_c², read here as a dense liquid of fractional instantons. The proposed test is to fit the 2+1-flavor ratio ℛ_π,a_0(T) to σ_s⁴/3,σ_s²/3,σ_s between 150 and 300 MeV.

Caveats are substantial, and the author flags them himself: - The ℱ_j are unknown, and the ansatz is called “rank supposition.” FRG work already indicates additional invariants are needed. - The non-degenerate case relevant to the proposed lattice test is deferred to a separate paper. - QCD is “blithely” assumed close to the Veneziano limit.

arXiv:2610.02169 — Drell–Yan lepton pair production from low to high transverse momentum (Benoît Assi et al.)

The prediction is N³LO matched to approximate N⁴LL′ q_T resummation, with unknown four-loop boundary terms estimated in large-β_0. Its main novelty is the nonperturbative input. The Collins–Soper kernel is taken from continuum-limit lattice QCD over 0.15≲b_T≲0.8 fm, giving c_0=0.032±0.012 GeV² at B_NP=2 GeV⁻¹. The only parameter fitted to Drell–Yan data is a Gaussian width, κ_NP=3.0±0.5 GeV⁻².

Comparison with ATLAS 13 TeV data: - Agreement: deviations are at most 1.3% below 10 GeV, 2.0% for 10–30 GeV, and 3.5% above 30 GeV, with χ²/bin of 0.2, 1.0 and 1.6 in those regions. - Lattice uncertainty: the c_0 uncertainty contributes up to 2.6% in the first bin and at most 0.8% elsewhere.

The calculation is transferred to event samples by maximum-entropy reweighting. Of 170 tabulated moments in r_T and ϕ_acop, 14–19 are selected, giving event-local multipliers ∝exp(∑λ_j g_j) that are strictly positive. - Sherpa: the reweighted sample matches the calculation to about 2% in a typical bin, against a prior that was off by up to 40%. The effective sample size is essentially unchanged (7.6% → 7.3%). - POWHEG: agreement is about 3% in a typical bin, with effective sample size held at 99%. The largest deviation from data below 200 GeV falls from 19% to 6%.

Caveats: - The prediction is about 8× less precise than the data in a typical bin, and PDF uncertainties (a few percent) are assessed elsewhere. - The moment covariance is treated as diagonal. - Positivity applies to the multiplier; the Sherpa prior itself retains signed weights. - Between 200 and 900 GeV the ungated POWHEG weight overshoots the data by 4–40%. - Extension to W production is proposed but not done, which matters for any m_W application.

arXiv:2610.01825 — Near Threshold Kaluza-Klein Graviton Decays and the Dark Dimension (Kevin Langhoff)

On shell, the massive cubic KK-graviton vertex reduces to the double copy of the Yang–Mills vertex evaluated at massive momenta. The mass term cancels against the terms, and the cancellation follows from the field redefinition h=e^H-1. As a result the amplitude vanishes at threshold, and the decay is pure d-wave with Γ∝p⁵∝Q⁵/2. Relative to the s-wave rate assumed in the dark-dimension cascade literature, the suppression is ∼(Q/μ)²∼10⁻²⁴ for Q∼1 meV and GeV parents.

Consequences for the flat dark dimension: - Cascade: summing over a flat tower with the completeness bound on g_mnℓ saturated, the mass-distribution peak moves by less than 0.1% by matter–radiation equality (δn=100, R=0.05–0.2 μm). - Dark matter: GeV-scale gravitons then live only ∼10⁵ yr, which excludes KK gravitons as the dark matter. - Irreducible background: freeze-in still produces ρ_h/ρ_DM=1.3×10⁻⁶⁽T_RH/5 MeV)³⁽m_KK/5 meV)⁻¹. COMPTEL and EGRET MeV gamma-ray data then cap T_RH. - Combined bound: with T_RH≥5.96 MeV from BBN+CMB+BAO, a viable window survives only for R≲0.2 μm (m_KK≳1 eV). That is roughly three orders of magnitude below the R∼Λ⁻¹/4 expectation.

Caveats: the analysis covers flat or weakly warped geometries only, and the cascade estimate uses a saturated coupling bound. The threshold suppression was found independently by Lee, Randall and Riojas (the Wednesday paper). A factor-10 improvement in MeV telescopes such as AMEGO-X or e-ASTROGAM would tighten the bound further.

Citation radar

The radar this week is a single entry, but it points at the dominant story in direct detection right now: LZ’s lone 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate (3.4σ local, 2.6σ global, non-blind). The reference list shows the interpretation wave already moving on from “which model fits” to “which observable kills which model.” Solar capture, the high-energy sideband, annual modulation and alternative targets are now where the arguments are being settled.

arXiv:2609.06153 — Exothermic dark matter and the 248 keV nuclear recoil in LUX-ZEPLIN (Howard Baer et al.)

Baer and Barger propose the downscattering alternative to the endothermic Higgsino reading. In their model, the relic is the heavier state of a pseudo-Dirac pair split by |δ| ≃ 350 keV. Because there is no threshold speed, the predicted count shifts by only 0.3% as v_esc runs from 500 to 600 km/s. The endothermic count, by contrast, swings from zero to 143× its central value.

Several constraints follow from the setup: - Mediator. Weak-strength coupling overproduces the event by ~10⁶, which forces a dark-photon mediator. - Splitting. Longevity of the excited state requires |δ| < 2mₑ. - Excited fraction. A coupled-channel calculation (the Born approximation violates unitarity here) gives an excited fraction of 2×10⁻³ to 4×10⁻², which implies ε ~ 10⁻⁶ at a 1 GeV mediator. - Ground state. Upscattering of the ground state excludes |δ| ≲ 300 keV, so the endothermic readings appear as the small-splitting limit of the same model.

The headline test is argon: it predicts ~4–6 events per tonne-year near 250 keV, where the endothermic reading is forbidden at any exposure. It also predicts percent-level rather than near-total annual modulation.

At 44 citations since its September posting, it has likely become the default citation for the exothermic branch. It is one of three exothermic treatments the authors identify, alongside many endothermic ones. It also supplies the quantitative halo-sensitivity argument against endpoint tuning and a sharp discriminator that DEAP-3600 and DarkSide-50 could apply to existing data. That reading is inferred; the citing papers aren’t visible here.

item.title: Thursday, October 1, 2026
item.description:
Small corrections, real consequences

Gaggero et al. arXiv:2609.40229 compute the three-loop 𝒪(αα_s²⁾ mixed QCD-EW piece of the top pole-to-MS relation. They find a −216 MeV shift in m_t(M_t), roughly the size of the quoted experimental error. That paper sets the day’s pattern. Several papers find effects that look like footnotes but are as large as the uncertainties people quote. This is the same lesson as Monday’s ρπ helicity-convention fix, now spread across lattice PDFs and fit statistics. On the LZ side, Luengas et al. close most of the thermal electroweak-multiplet space under the Standard Halo Model. The LMC tail that Bozorgnia et al. raised yesterday is again the escape route.

Themes

Corrections the size of errors

  • Gluon quasi-PDFs. Monahan et al. arXiv:2609.40205 trace a finite polynomial in the Balitsky–Morris–Radyushkin gluon matching kernel to a transverse-index contraction over 2 rather than d-2. Fixing it moves the extracted normalized second and third gluon moments by 11–13%.
  • Fit statistics. Csanád et al. arXiv:2609.40019 show Neyman-χ² biases of about -3/λ in histogram ratios. These biases do not shrink with finer binning, which matters for femtoscopy.
  • Dark-photon acceptance. Zhong et al. arXiv:2609.40052 find that the choice of production model shifts NA62 dark-photon acceptance by more than 30% at fixed yield, so it cannot be treated as a simple rate rescaling.
  • A clean null. Harris et al. arXiv:2609.39582 find that single-diffractive W/Z production biases m_W by at most 1.58 MeV.

Solar capture squeezes the multiplets

Luengas et al. arXiv:2609.38316 generalize the Higgsino solar-capture analysis to higher representations. IceCube requires δ≳350 keV up to 100 TeV, which rules out most thermal multiplets as the source of the LZ event under the SHM. An LMC-like tail lifts the preferred splitting back above the bound for many of them. Roy et al. arXiv:2609.40234 offer an elastic bino/singlino route through the Higgsino asymmetry X, which escapes the inelastic-splitting problem. Meissner et al. arXiv:2609.39529 return with supermassive charged gravitinos. Their reading predicts microsecond-spaced multiple recoils along a straight track, which is at least a sharp test.

Tauonic penguins and R(D*)

Baltà et al. arXiv:2609.40072 map the SMEFT regions favored by R(D⁽*)) and the enhanced B⁺→K⁺νν̅ rate. In those regions, b→sττ rates can rise by orders of magnitude, and they break degeneracies that Kνν̅ alone cannot. This follows yesterday’s Belle II WET reinterpretation. On the experimental-method side, Xiao et al. arXiv:2609.39998 show that the sPlot-based amplitude extraction for B→Kπμμ still works with non-factorizing efficiency and background.

Faster sums, fewer categories

  • Colour sums. Frederix et al. arXiv:2609.39574 apply symmetric-group FFTs to colour sums, cutting the 11-gluon case from about 1700 s to 0.8 s.
  • Event weighting. Yang et al. arXiv:2609.38189 replace sensitivity categories with continuous S/B weights, demonstrated on CMS Open Data diphotons.
  • LLM-guided searches. Elsharkawy et al.’s hAIthem arXiv:2609.38309 pairs an RL agent pretrained on Lagrangians with LLM agents that propose signatures. It extends yesterday’s LLM-in-the-loop cluster from calculation to model space.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.40229: A −216 MeV mixed QCD-EW shift in the top mass relation, comparable to the experimental error. Elliptic periods appear along the way.
  • arXiv:2609.40205: Argues the true MS lattice gluon is harder than reported, and that the |x|>1 exterior carries no independent physics.
  • arXiv:2609.38316: The general-representation solar bound, which is now the reference test for any heavy-multiplet LZ fit.
  • arXiv:2609.39574: Three orders of magnitude on colour sums using standard partial amplitudes. Generator authors will notice.
  • arXiv:2609.40019: Short, analytic, and directly actionable: use the likelihood for ratio fits.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.40237 First double-differential cross-section measurements in proton multiplicity and kinematics for mesonless νμ CC interactions on argon — MicroBooNE collaboration et al. (hep-ex). No generator describes the proton multiplicities, which is unwelcome news for the low-energy-excess modelling.
  • arXiv:2609.38233 XENONnT pp-Dominated Solar Neutrinos Constrain the ν1 Pseudo-Dirac Splitting — Gio Leone (hep-ph). Excludes δm_1²≳5.9×10⁻¹³ eV² at 2σ.
  • arXiv:2609.40008 PINNing the pion — Mayank Goel et al. (hep-ph). Finds a_μ^ππ=506.48(2.02)(1.70)×10⁻¹⁰ with analyticity built into the loss.
  • arXiv:2609.39158 Heavy Dark Baryons at Large N — Giovani Dalla Valle Garcia et al. (hep-ph). Van der Waals self-interactions span dwarf-to-cluster velocities and point to GeV-scale dark baryons. A companion paper is arXiv:2609.39193.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.40229 — 𝒪(αα_s²⁾ corrections to the Top Quark mass (Daniele Gaggero et al.)

The first three-loop mixed QCD–EW term in the top pole-to-MS relation shifts m_t(M_t) by −216 MeV at M_t=172.3 GeV. The pure 𝒪(α_s³⁾ term shifts it by −554 MeV, so the mixed term is about 0.5% of the “NLO” result, comparable to the QCD piece. The total NLO→NNLO shift is −770 MeV, leaving M_t-m_t⁽ⁿ⁼²⁾⁽M_t)=106 MeV. Across the full M_t range the shift is a steady ~200 MeV, against the ATLAS+CMS uncertainty of ±0.33 GeV. The calculation uses the Jegerlehner–Kalmykov scheme with tadpoles kept, so the MS mass is gauge invariant. Master integrals are built in ϵ-factorized form. The W topologies contain the two-loop-sunrise elliptic period, and the Z/H topologies contain the three-loop equal-mass banana. Several required forms do not survive into the physical result: the weight-four modular form and ℱ_1. γ_5 traces in the χ-Goldstone diagrams are handled with local counterterms. The authors check the RGE-predicted poles, the Yukawa consistency of the single pole, and the NNLO QCD top width extracted from the imaginary part.

Why it matters: the term is the same size as the experimental error. In the effective series that groups the one-loop QCD and EW pieces together, the scale band shrinks from 175.2⁺⁹.2_-7.9 GeV to 172.1⁺².4_-5.0 GeV.

Caveats: the residual band is still several GeV wide and asymmetric. The authors also warn that the known, sizable 𝒪(α²⁾ corrections are left out of their mass-scan plot.

arXiv:2609.40205 — Unpolarized quasi- and pseudo-distributions at one loop: gluon correlator decomposition, matching, and the region |x|>1 (Christopher Monahan et al.)

The Balitsky–Morris–Radyushkin gluon-in-gluon kernel misses a finite polynomial. The polynomial is the same in all three of their index combinations. The authors trace it to one appendix step, where a loop-generated index between the two field strengths is summed over 2 transverse directions instead of d-2. That drops an evanescent operator, which produces exactly the missing polynomial when it multiplies the collinear pole. Their MS result agrees with Yao–Ji–Zhang, and the same polynomial separates Yao–Ji–Zhang from BMR. In ratio-scheme pseudo-PDF extractions, ⟨x⟩_g is protected. The normalized second and third moments, however, come out roughly 11% and 13% too low at α_s=0.3, so the true MS gluon is harder than reported.

The framework splits the correlator into six covariant form factors with a 6×6 mixing matrix. That matrix has three eigenvalue sectors (Z_⊥⊥², Z_⊥⊥Z_∥⊥, Z_∥⊥²), so any lattice index choice follows without new loops. The result is cross-checked in R_ξ and axial gauge.

A second conceptual result uses Paley–Wiener. The |x|>1 exterior comes entirely from the branch point of log(z̃²μ²⁾ at ν=0, and at leading power it is fixed pointwise by the renormalization group. At one loop it is n_f-independent, with tail coefficients 5C_A/6 for ℳ_pp and 11C_A/6 for 𝒢^ziiz. Fitting the exterior with independent parameters therefore risks absorbing power corrections into the leading-twist PDF.

Caveats: the analysis is one-loop only, the moment shifts are an estimate at fixed α_s, and gluon target-mass corrections are not known.

arXiv:2609.38316 — Constraints on Complex Electroweak WIMPs from Solar Capture (Juan P. Luengas et al.)

Endothermic capture depends only on hypercharge: the Y=1 rate is 4× the Y=1/2 rate. For n≥4, the loop-induced SI elastic scattering (∝n⁴) and the Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation keep the Sun in equilibrium. The IceCube bound is therefore a single universal curve per Y for fermions and scalars alike.

The excluded splitting is largest at TeV masses, ~600 keV for Y=1 and ~570 keV for Y=1/2, and it falls to 350–400 keV by 100 TeV. Under the SHM this excludes the 3_1, 5_1, 4_1/2 and 6_1/2 as sources of the LZ 248 keV event. The 8_1/2 is marginal. Only the 10_1/2 (158 TeV) and 12_1/2 (253 TeV) survive, because they sit in the heavy-mass LZ island.

The solar curve barely depends on the halo, since capture is dominated by slow particles. The LMC tail instead moves the LZ-preferred δ above 500 keV. Under that tail, 6_1/2 and above become allowed, 4_1/2 is marginal, and 3_1, 5_1 escape IceCube but match LZ only at ~3σ.

For the doublets: - The fermion doublet reproduces the earlier Higgsino bound, δ≲566 keV. - The scalar doublet has no spin-dependent sinking channel and stalls at 0.1–0.2 R_⊙. Its bound peaks near 510 keV and is gone by 10 TeV.

Why it matters: it makes the velocity-tail question decisive for any heavy-multiplet LZ fit.

Caveats: - The fit rests on a single event, and its two mass islands are separated by only 1–2σ. - Sommerfeld factors are parametric, good to ~30% off resonance. - The analysis restricts to Y≤1 and assumes no tree-level Higgs portal for scalars. A portal with λ_χH≳0.01 would strengthen the scalar-doublet bound.

item.title: Wednesday, September 30, 2026
item.description:
JUNO leans normal

JUNO arXiv:2609.37895 is the day’s firmest result. It uses 207 live days and 8,294 IBD candidates. The measurement gives Δm²_31 to about 1% and the best solar parameters yet. Adding the long-baseline Δm²_31 constraints favors normal ordering at ≥2.1σ for any CP phase, with a Bayes factor of 10.2. That is an indication, not a determination, and the collaboration says so.

On the flavor side, last week’s standing question about the LHCb beauty-strange state already has a quantitative answer. Albaladejo et al. arXiv:2609.38022 predicted it before the measurement. The LZ recoil drew five papers again, this time on halos and decaying parents.

Themes

LZ: the LMC and decaying parents

Bozorgnia et al. arXiv:2609.36184 extend Tuesday’s halo turn. The LMC-induced tail pushes endothermic fits to larger splittings, where collider and indirect limits bite harder. Elastic readings are mostly unaffected. Chanda et al. arXiv:2609.36814 read the event as a ~340 keV hyperfine excitation of atomic DM. That predicts xenon near threshold, tungsten open, and nothing on Ar or Ge.

Jho et al. offer two routes to a nonstandard flux: - A decaying parent could supply boosted upscatterers arXiv:2609.37545. - A decaying parent could instead replenish exothermic downscatterers arXiv:2609.37561. This version predicts a 700–810 keV line in argon, which is testable.

ANTARES’s full-dataset solar WIMP null (Albert et al. arXiv:2609.37422) adds another solar-capture dataset alongside the IceCube and Super-K limits.

Four-loop evolution, and non-global logs

Gehrmann et al. arXiv:2609.37563 compute the four-loop pure-singlet P_qq analytically, which completes the quark-to-quark splitting function. It comes a day after Moch’s non-singlet completion. Becher et al. arXiv:2609.35972 give the first NLL non-global resummation for jet-vetoed Higgs production using MARZILI, the framework behind yesterday’s super-leading-log work. Hard matching dominates their uncertainty. Giuli arXiv:2609.37556 follows up on resummation-scale effects in PDF fits.

LLMs inside the calculation

This is new as a cluster. Camarda et al. arXiv:2609.37238 report closed-form NLO helicity cross sections for V+jet, built largely by Claude agents and documented down to token budgets. He et al. arXiv:2609.36007 have an LLM design local IR subtraction, validated against EERAD3 on a laptop. Mikhasenko arXiv:2609.37716 releases the first public reproduction of Godfrey–Isgur, including an agent-accessible interface.

Spectroscopy gets interpreted

Albaladejo et al. arXiv:2609.38022 use lattice-constrained coupled channels with no LHCb input. Their prediction lands within 1.1–1.7σ of the observed peak. It describes the state as a B̅K bound state with a width of tens of keV. Khemchandani et al. arXiv:2609.37653 recast the glueball candidate X(2370) as ϕh_1(1380) dynamics.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.37895: JUNO gives the first reactor-plus-accelerator indication of normal ordering, plus world-leading Δm²_31 precision.
  • arXiv:2609.38022: A lattice-fixed prediction of LHCb’s state that effectively answers its mass-deficit question. It also predicts the 1⁺ partner’s mass.
  • arXiv:2609.37563: The complete four-loop P_qq, analytic for all x, which is direct input to N³LO evolution.
  • arXiv:2609.37238: A speed-up of more than 10⁵ for A_0–A_7 predictions. The methods section on agentic LLM use is worth reading for its own sake.
  • arXiv:2609.36234: Lee et al. find KK-graviton decays suppressed by (q/m_n)². They argue this rules out existing Dark Dimension cascade models.

From the community

  • arXiv:2609.37117 Input to the SCAC Facilities Subcommittee from the U.S. Muon Collider Collaboration — S. Jindariani et al. (physics.acc-ph). The muon-collider case for US facilities planning over 2026–2036. It is a counterpart to last week’s FCC public-debate pieces.
  • arXiv:2609.35830 Translating LHCb’s Documentation — Andy Morris et al. (physics.ed-ph). About 22% of Starterkit visits now reach a Mandarin page, which is a concrete onboarding data point.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.37146 Measurements of electroweak penguin B decays with missing energy at Belle and Belle II — Lorenz Gärtner (hep-ex). A WET reinterpretation of B⁺→K⁺νν̅ prefers an enhanced vector contribution.
  • arXiv:2609.36369 tt̅ spin correlations from toponium production scenarios… — A. Cota Rodríguez et al. (hep-ph). Spin correlations are proposed as the discriminator between toponium and non-relativistic resummation.
  • arXiv:2609.32479 Fast and Precise Learned Charged-Particle Trajectory Regression at the Large Hadron Collider — Jonathan Renusch et al. (cs.LG). The authors claim the first learned track fit at full Kalman precision.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.37895 — Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering (The JUNO Collaboration)

JUNO used 207.2 live days, 8,294 IBD candidates, and a 52.5 km mean baseline. It measures Δm²_31 = +2.509⁺⁰.027_-0.025×10⁻³ eV² under NO and -2.482⁺⁰.025_-0.026×10⁻³ eV² under IO, a precision of about 1% with Feldman–Cousins intervals. It also reports sin²θ_12 = 0.3036±0.0064 (2.1%) and Δm²_21 = (7.388±0.078)×10⁻⁵ eV² (1.1%).

This is the first analysis to fold in TAO near-detector data (90,280 IBDs) alongside Daya Bay for the unoscillated spectrum. Three independent groups ran blinded analyses, and their results were consistent.

The mass-ordering statement is a reactor–accelerator tension test. NuFit long-baseline Δm²_31 pulls under each hypothesis give Δχ²_IO-NO = 4.86. Pseudo-experiments that scan δ_CP turn this into p = 0.0197, or 2.1σ one-sided (2.3σ two-sided). An independent Bayesian MCMC gives κ= 10.18.

The caveats are structural: - JUNO alone cannot pick the minimum. Its Δχ² profile has several degenerate local minima in Δm²_31. The Daya Bay constraint is what selects the physical one; JUNO then sets the precision. - The NMO evidence is not JUNO-internal. It rests on the mismatch with long-baseline experiments. - Systematics are starting to matter. Statistics still dominate, but Bi–Po backgrounds and detection efficiency are now significant contributors. - Energy resolution is slightly worse than simulated. It is about 3.5% at the ⁶⁸Ge peak, a bit above the MC prediction.

A by-product is the world’s largest geoneutrino sample, at 73±11 TNU.

arXiv:2609.38022 — The new LHCb beauty-strange state as the bottom partner of the D_s0^*(2317) (Miguel Albaladejo et al.)

LHCb’s narrow B̅_s⁰π⁰ peak sits at 5698.9±1.5±0.6 MeV, 74 MeV below the B⁻K⁺ threshold, with 343 signal candidates. Two unitarized coupled-channel models were tested against it: - Model I: leading-order Weinberg–Tomozawa plus a bare bs̅ state, fitted to B̅⁽*)K lattice levels. - Model II: NLO HMChPT, with its low-energy constants fixed by charm-sector lattice scattering lengths and carried over by heavy-quark flavor symmetry.

Isospin breaking enters through physical masses, π⁰–η mixing and m_u≠m_d, and adds no free parameters.

Predictions with no LHCb input land 1.1σ (Model II) and 1.3–1.7σ (Model I) from the observed mass. Freeing one parameter (the cutoff Λ or the subtraction constant a_b) reproduces the zero-width reference fit, with χ²/dof = 1.22 for 84 degrees of freedom. The required shifts are about 1.1–1.3σ, and joint fits with the lattice data cost only Δχ²_LQCD ≈ 1.1–2.5.

Properties of the state in the fitted models:

Quantity Model I Model II
B̅K compositeness ~45–50% ~60%
Isospin-violating width 34 keV 82.5 keV
1⁺ partner mass 5748.8 MeV 5751.7 MeV

The factor of two between the widths is a rough measure of model dependence, and radiative decays are not included.

The key point is the 1⁺–0⁺ splitting of 49–52 MeV, which is essentially the B_s^*–B_s mass difference (49.4 MeV). The observed peak therefore cannot discriminate between the two assignments and may contain both states. B̅_s⁰γ searches are the direct test.

The authors are careful on several points: - A good fit does not prove a molecular state. - The lattice inputs are at unphysical quark masses, and the predictions carry no systematic uncertainties. - The same NLO amplitudes are in tension with ALICE Dπ femtoscopy in the charm sector. - The resolution kernel was extracted from LHCb’s published figure.

arXiv:2609.37563 — The four-loop quark-to-quark splitting function in QCD (Thomas Gehrmann et al.)

This paper gives the first fully analytic, all-x four-loop pure-singlet P_ps⁽³⁾. Combined with the non-singlet result (cited here as the same authors’ arXiv:2604.09534), it completes P_qq at N³LO.

The method follows these steps: 1. Compute off-shell quark operator matrix elements, including mixing with gluon and gauge-variant operators. 2. Reduce integrals by IBP over finite fields and solve differential equations in an auxiliary parameter t to reach high Mellin moments. 3. Fit an ansatz of harmonic sums up to weight six to those moments. 4. Invert the Mellin transform to harmonic polylogarithms up to weight six.

The result reproduces the known fixed moments through n=22. It also reproduces the ζ_3 contribution at n=2 that arises from a spurious (n-2) pole.

New content includes the previously unknown leading-power small-x coefficients of lnx/x and 1/x. There is also a discrepancy with the double-log resummation of Davies et al.: the ζ_2ln⁴ x coefficient lacks a (d_F^abcd)²/N_c term there. The two agree at leading colour, matching the pattern seen in the non-singlet case, and the origin is unexplained.

The practical impact on evolution is modest. The existing moment-based approximation agrees with the exact result within its uncertainties over 10⁻⁵<x<1. The main gain is that the approximation uncertainty for this entry of the evolution matrix is gone, while the gluon entries remain approximate.

The ancillary files include a numerical fit accurate to 10⁻⁵ absolute and 10⁻⁸ relative. The exact γ_qq⁽³⁾ may also help reconstruct γ_gg⁽³⁾ through reciprocity.

item.title: Tuesday, September 29, 2026
item.description:
A helicity convention, corrected

The day’s cleanest result is Žlebčík arXiv:2609.31828. The ρ→ππ helicity convention in the time-dependent B⁰→(ρπ)⁰ Dalitz analyses does not match the one the downstream isospin analysis assumes. Correcting it drops the direct-versus-indirect α tension from 2.9σ to 2.1σ. LZ produced no papers yesterday and seven today, and the new work is mostly about the velocity distribution rather than the particle content. Underneath, ML papers now read as infrastructure reports, and several precision-QCD results arrive together.

Themes

The LZ recoil meets the halo

Oliveira arXiv:2609.35650 rebuilds LZ’s inference and allows a surviving excited-state fraction f. For f≳10⁻⁵–10⁻² exothermic scattering dominates, and at f=1/2 the required cross section falls by factors of 80 to 1.6×10⁴. Das et al. arXiv:2609.35737 use a Gaia-informed halo with a suppressed high-velocity tail. Exothermic readings barely move, while endothermic ones need larger cross sections and smaller splittings, and the LMC partly restores the tail. This extends O’Hare’s halo null from last week. Model-building continues with Centelles Chuliá et al.’s Majoron-mediated 𝒪_6 arXiv:2609.32435 and Pallis’s 0.1 PeV higgsino arXiv:2609.33869. The testable addition is Dutra et al. arXiv:2609.33952: if the excited state decays radiatively, a sub-MeV line at E_γ≃δ falls within COSI’s reach.

CKM through careful bookkeeping

Feldmann et al. arXiv:2609.34696 build soft-collinear ChPT for B→π at large recoil. Its chiral logs are incompatible with Hard-Pion ChPT. On first-row unitarity, Gialidi et al. arXiv:2609.31834 find that only FCC-ee fully decouples V_ud from SMEFT left-handed currents. Hayen arXiv:2609.32873 argues that the β-recoil spectrum is clean enough to serve as a BSM laboratory. Both continue the V_ud thread that Seng’s δ_C framework reopened on 09-18.

ML as plumbing

Vami et al. arXiv:2609.31739 report that CMS’s AXOL1TL and CICADA triggers selected more than four billion events in 2024. Tong et al. arXiv:2609.35755 address systematics in the latent spaces those searches rely on. Kakati et al. arXiv:2609.31862 train one tokenized model in which particle flow and simulation are just different directions through shared weights. The quietest useful paper is Sakuma’s Hypothesis-awkward arXiv:2609.31820, which has found 37 bugs in Awkward Array so far.

Precision QCD, on several fronts

Chala arXiv:2609.33448 completes the SM thermal masses at 𝒪(g⁶⁾, direct input to last week’s phase-transition thread. Moch arXiv:2609.34837 reports that the non-singlet four-loop splitting functions are complete. Abdolmaleki et al. arXiv:2609.35344 include resummation-scale uncertainty in PDF fits for the first time and find it matters for LHC observables.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.31828: A convention mismatch worth 0.8σ, giving α=(87.0⁺¹¹.8_-4.7)^∘. Any isospin analysis built on a Dalitz fit should check its conventions.
  • arXiv:2609.35650: LZ’s published intervals do not cover pseudo-Dirac halos. A χ_1-only benchmark sits 30× above the limit if half the halo is χ_2.
  • arXiv:2609.34984: Schalch gives the first Monte Carlo resummation of super-leading logarithms, a route to putting Glauber exchange into parton showers.
  • arXiv:2609.31833: Akita et al. show that momentum-averaged treatments can get the sign of ΔN_eff wrong for strongly nonthermal neutrinos.
  • arXiv:2609.33151: Freese finds that the D-term sign follows the spin of the binding field, not mechanical stability. That makes the negative hadronic D-term the thing that needs explaining.

From the community

  • arXiv:2609.32307 Hydrogen mon amour — Christophe Grojean et al. (physics.soc-ph). The essay asks whether hydrogen could cover renewable gaps in the FCC’s 1.3 TWh/yr supply. It pairs with last week’s Janot et al. climate piece.
  • arXiv:2609.32874 Machine learning for the LHC physics program: a 2025-2026 stocktake — Jesse Thaler (hep-ph). Most of the text was written by an agentic AI pipeline reading 569 papers. The method is as interesting as the headline claim that HEPML is now infrastructure.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.33990 First measurement of the antihydrogen production cross section through the charge-exchange reaction of low-energy antiprotons with orthopositronium — GBAR Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). The measured values agree with three-body theory.
  • arXiv:2609.35133 The Dπ and D^π femtoscopy puzzle* — Pablo Encarnación et al. (hep-ph). ALICE’s extracted scattering parameters depend on the choice of fitting window.
  • arXiv:2609.34364 NNLO QCD Corrections to η_t→HZ — Cai-Ping Jia et al. (hep-ph). The toponium width converges slowly, with NNLO at 52% of LO.
  • arXiv:2609.34155 Comment on “Fermi-LAT Galactic Center Excess Morphology…” — Kevork N. Abazajian et al. (astro-ph.HE). The original maps squared the projected mass instead of computing ∫ρ².

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.31828 — Impact of Helicity–Isospin Convention Matching on the Extraction of α from B⁰→(ρπ)⁰ (Radek \v{Z}leb\v{c}ík)

Belle and BaBar both define the ρ→ππ helicity angles in the cyclic convention, in which the ρ⁰ angle is referenced to the π⁻. They then extract α with the Lipkin–Nir–Quinn–Snyder relation A⁺⁺A⁻⁺²A⁰. That relation holds only if the ρ⁰ angle is referenced to the π⁺. The mismatch amounts to a sign flip of A⁰ and A̅⁰. Žlebčík corrects it by flipping the 12 of the 26 U/I parameters that are linear in A⁰ or A̅⁰, along with the corresponding covariance off-diagonals. He first reproduces the public HFLAV ρπ and combined curves exactly, then reruns the scan.

The corrected ρπ curve is much flatter near 90°. Its tension with the indirect value (91.2°) drops from 2.9σ to 2.1σ. The combined result becomes α=(87.0⁺¹¹.8_-4.7)^∘, compared with HFLAV’s (84.1⁺³.7_-3.0)^∘. The ππ+ρρ combination alone gives (85.9⁺⁸.6_-3.9)^∘.

The paper says every phenomenological treatment it examined carries the mismatch, including the Belle and BaBar papers, HFLAV/CKMfitter and UTfit. It traces the root cause to Snyder–Quinn never specifying the reference pion.

Caveats: - The apparent precision was partly an artefact. The combined upper error roughly triples, and ρπ no longer improves precision; only the 2σ interval tightens slightly, to [79.1°, 108.1°]. - The ρπ best-fit χ² rises from 8.4 to 9.5 (17 dof), although the combined χ² improves by 1.4. - A mirror solution near 0° persists.

For Belle II and LHCb, the practical lesson is that the Dalitz convention must be fixed before the isospin fit.

arXiv:2609.35650 — The LZ event with a two-state dark matter halo (Vinicius Oliveira)

Oliveira rebuilds LZ’s inference from public material. He uses a binned likelihood from the Fig. 5 projection (3 S1c slices × 32 bins), the shell-model nuclear response, and a toy-MC Neyman construction. The Helm form factor would overestimate the rate at 248 keV by a factor of 5, which is why the shell-model response matters. The recast matches LZ’s endothermic upper limits within 26% at all 17 points with δ ≥ 50 keV, and within 5% at about half of them. Its local significances run 0.2–0.7σ low: Z = 2.5 versus 3.0 at 1 TeV and δ = 300 keV.

The recast then allows a surviving excited-state fraction f. Freeze-out or freeze-in naturally gives f≈1/2 unless χ_2 decays. Exothermic scattering dominates above a critical f of 6×10⁻³, 1.4×10⁻³ and 3×10⁻⁵ at δ = 250, 300 and 350 keV. Above that point the required cross section scales as 1/f.

At f=1/2 and 1 TeV: - The best-fit σ_N drops by 80, 360 and 1.6×10⁴ at those three splittings. - σ_N stays within 3.5×10⁻⁴⁵–3.6×10⁻⁴⁴ cm² over 250–500 keV. - The endothermic cutoff disappears. - Di Mauro’s thermal benchmark (297 keV, 6.5×10⁻⁴³ cm²) sits 30× above the upper limit.

Caveats: - The exothermic intervals cannot be validated against any LZ result. - The likelihood is binned and the background is fixed. - Only the Standard Halo Model is used, which connects to Das et al. on halo dependence. - The paper does not impose the χ_2 lifetime bound. Radiative decay could drive f→0, which is exactly what Dutra et al. propose to test with a line in COSI. - The paper also flags unexplained internal inconsistencies in where LZ’s published lower limits turn on.

arXiv:2609.34984 — A First Glimpse at Super-Leading Logarithms in Monte Carlo Evolution (Nicolas Schalch)

Schalch extends the EFT-based Marzili framework to resum the SLL tower α_sⁿ⁺³L²ⁿ⁺³. The tower comes from two Glauber exchanges, arbitrarily many incoming-collinear emissions, and one terminal soft emission into the gap. The calculation is at the leading nonzero colour order, relative 1/N_c². The RG path-ordered exponential is turned into a shower-like sequence of Sudakov-sampled emissions acting on paired amplitude and conjugate-amplitude colour flows.

The key technical point is that retaining h=d+p≤2 bounds the flow mismatch to at most two partner swaps at any multiplicity. Glauber interference therefore survives without the colour space blowing up. In qq′, any real emission between the Glaubers gives zero. In qg, such emissions and unequal final flows contribute.

The validation is against analytic resummations at ΔY=2, ξ=α_sL²⁼⁸:

Channel Marzili Analytic
Octet (qq′) C_O=6.2759(47) 6.2754
Singlet (qq′) C_S=-11.6853(45) −11.6804
qg→qV C_qg=0.1099(247) 0.0971

The pronounced qg turnover is reproduced.

Caveats: - The calculation uses fixed coupling, strict-forward geometry and a single soft emission. The NGL–SLL interplay is not yet included. - There is a real sign problem in qg: the mean absolute weight is about 52× the mean signed weight, hence the ~25% error. - A mapping to CVolver’s cutoff-regulated Coulomb treatment is still open.

A parallel parton-shower effort (Helliwell) is noted.

The full texts of arXiv:2609.31833 and arXiv:2609.33151 were not supplied, so they are not expanded here.
